result_and_mechanism_map.title: A natural Hilbert-Polya object must explain zero statistics without encoding the zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates average zero density from oscillatory statistics, uses GUE-type spacing as evidence for a spectral model, and imposes a naturality test that rules out constructing the space directly from the zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Function-field Frobenius turns the periodic-orbit minus sign into cohomological absorption
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transfers the problem to positive-characteristic global fields, where Frobenius eigenvalues, Riemann-Roch, Lefschetz, and positivity provide a tested dictionary; the alternating cohomology sign suggests that the desired Hilbert space must appear negatively, as missing rather than emitted spectral lines.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The adele-class quotient makes the idele action canonical
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies X=A/k* from the quotient-space/noncommutative-algebra dictionary and shows why dividing by k* is exactly what permits the idele class group to act.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two vanishing conditions and periodization embed adele-class functions into the regular representation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds the weighted L2 space by killing the fixed-point and divergent integral modes, periodizes Schwartz functions into functions on C_k, and shows that the resulting isometry is equivariant up to the half-density factor; its cokernel is the proposed Polya-Hilbert space.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The cokernel generator detects critical zeros but delta truncates multiplicity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Decomposes by compact idele-class characters, obtains a generator with discrete imaginary spectrum at critical-line zeros, and states a trace formula over those zeros without first defining the L-functions in the construction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exact sequences express absorption as a regular representation minus the zero spectrum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the two removed modes and the cokernel sequence to write the formal character of functions on X as trivial terms minus the critical-zero trace, exposing both the absorption sign and the need for regularization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lefschetz trace is a distributional restriction of a kernel to the diagonal
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the inverse-determinant contribution of an isolated transverse fixed point and shows how alternating bundle traces recover the usual cohomological Lefschetz formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A flow trace splits into periodic-orbit and stationary-point terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Pushes the pulled-back graph distribution to the time variable and identifies contributions from closed orbits and zeros of the vector field, each weighted by the transverse return determinant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier convolution justifies the local fixed-point factor
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For multiplication by a local-field element, replaces a formally ill-defined product of delta distributions by convolution of their Fourier transforms and recovers the inverse absolute-value factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dual support cutoffs regularize the local multiplicative trace
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines position and Fourier cutoffs, computes the operator symbol, separates the logarithmically divergent identity term, and identifies the finite remainder with the unique principal-value distribution whose Fourier transform vanishes at one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Places appear as codimension-one fixed hyperplanes in the adele-class space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Classifies nontrivial isotropy by vanishing of one adelic coordinate, identifies its transverse action with multiplication on the corresponding local field, and formally sums the local terms into Weil's explicit distribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A non-type-I S-local quotient still admits an intrinsic L2 space and unitary Fourier transform
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses S-units to form a finite-place model retaining the global quotient pathology, proves convergence of the periodized inner product, and extends Fourier transform to the quotient L2 space so dual cutoffs are meaningful.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Selberg-style kernel summation yields exactly one principal-value term per selected place
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States and proves the S-local cutoff trace formula, lifting the test function to the idele product, summing quotient kernels, using Fourier symbols, and controlling the aggregate tail uniformly over S-units.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Removing delta changes off-line zeros from omissions into resonances
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why direct cutoff on unweighted L2(X) eliminates multiplicity truncation and admits every zero: critical zeros remain spectral points while noncritical zeros act through harmonic potential on the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Commuting time-frequency projectors identify the exact finite-dimensional cutoff space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: In positive characteristic, decomposes by compact characters, computes the trace and dimension, constructs basis vectors localized together with their Fourier transforms, and concludes that the two projections commute for large cutoff.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The global cutoff trace formula is equivalent to positivity of Weil's distribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Passes from stabilized S-local cutoff spaces to a global projection and proves that the conjectural trace identity implies a positive-type defect distribution, hence RH for every Grossencharacter L-function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Harmonic measure is the spectral footprint of an off-critical zero
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Computes the cutoff defect independently from RH: a zero on the critical line contributes a point mass, whereas an off-line zero contributes its Poisson/harmonic measure on the line, with full multiplicity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prolate spheroidal modes replace impossible compact support at an Archimedean place
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the geometry of two projections and the Landau-Pollak-Slepian transition spectrum to define an approximate joint time-frequency subspace even though no nonzero function has compact support in both variables.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The average zero count is the deficit of scaling states under adelic periodization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Counts phase-space states for the Hamiltonian qp with dual cutoffs and finds the smooth Riemann zero-count term as missing states in the image of the periodization map, reinforcing the absorption rather than emission sign.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adele classes model Frobenius but the construction remains GL(1)-specific work in progress
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Clarifies gauge-quotient and class-field analogies, contrasts the absorption sign with competing qp counting, and sketches a GL(n) extension whose missing piece is again a Lefschetz trace formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Global L-functions normalize tensor products of local homogeneous distributions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines local homogeneous distributions, normalizes almost all non-Archimedean factors, and shows that the global adelic distribution differs from their tensor product by the Euler product L-function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adelic Poisson summation gives reciprocity and rapid decay for the periodization map
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses k as its own dual lattice to relate E(f)(x) to E(Ff)(1/x), proving rapid decay at both norm extremes and extending the Mellin identity with L-functions into the critical strip.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Band-limited approximate units reduce the cokernel analysis to compact spectral support
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs uniformly bounded convolution approximate identities in weighted Sobolev spaces and transfers them to the idele class group, permitting density arguments with compact Fourier support.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Orthogonality to periodized functions is equivalent to distributional support at L-function zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Decomposes the dual Sobolev space by compact characters, converts orthogonality through Mellin transforms into L(s) times a compactly supported distribution, and classifies solutions as derivatives of point masses at zeros; these become generalized eigenvectors and Jordan chains.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Localized spectral pieces assemble into the zero-sum trace
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a frequency partition and zero-count growth to prove integrated cokernel operators are trace class and computes their trace from the triangular zero blocks.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weil's zero sum equals trivial spectral terms plus normalized local fixed-point distributions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the Weil distribution, rewrites its spectral side in the paper's h-transform notation, and isolates one principal-value integral for every place, matching the formal adelic trace structure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier-normalized cutoff principal values coincide with Weil's local prescriptions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Checks non-Archimedean, real, and complex fields separately, then tracks the shift caused by changing the additive character; summing the different-idele shifts yields the global explicit formula in cutoff normalization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic growth uniquely normalizes Haar measure on a modulated group
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how continuous and discrete norm ranges acquire the same asymptotic normalization and why cocompact subgroup measures disintegrate compatibly.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Transversality makes delta-section pullback and trace restriction well-defined
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines generalized bundle sections, pushforward, wave-front-controlled pullback, and the conormal symbol of a submanifold, providing the coordinate-free condition behind restricting a graph kernel to the diagonal.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Poincare return determinant is the symbol of the pulled-back graph distribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies the kernel formalism to a flow, proves transversality is invertibility of one minus the transverse return map, and derives both closed-orbit and stationary-point contributions with covolume normalization.

section_argument_map.mathematical_role: States the spectral/geometric program, the local and S-local results, the open global equivalence, and the Hilbert-Polya/random-matrix motivation.

section_argument_map.label: I. Quantum chaos and the hypothetical Riemann flow
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Compares periodic-orbit and Euler-product oscillatory terms to infer prime periods, instability exponents, absence of time reversal, and two decisive mismatches.

section_argument_map.label: II. Algebraic geometry and positive-characteristic global fields
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses the Frobenius/cohomology dictionary to turn the troublesome minus sign into an absorption-spectrum clue and identifies the idele class group as the flow group.

section_argument_map.label: III. Spectral interpretation of critical zeros
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Constructs the adele-class Hilbert space, embeds it into the regular representation, and identifies a cokernel spectrum with critical L-function zeros subject to the artificial delta parameter.

section_argument_map.label: IV. Distribution trace formula for flows
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Derives fixed-point and periodic-orbit contributions to a distributional trace from Lefschetz transversality.

section_argument_map.label: V. Multiplicative action on a local field
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Makes the local fixed-point term rigorous with Fourier products, infrared/ultraviolet cutoffs, and a canonically normalized principal value.

section_argument_map.label: VI. Global formal trace computation
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Classifies fixed hyperplanes in the adele-class space, formally recovers the place terms of Weil's formula, and explains why positivity points to an L2 Lefschetz construction rather than quantization.

section_argument_map.label: VII. S-local trace formula
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Builds the non-type-I S-local quotient, extends Fourier transform to its L2 space, proves the cutoff trace formula, and controls the global sum of local error terms.

section_argument_map.label: VIII. Global trace formula and elimination of delta
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Defines the canonical cutoff, proves the function-field equivalence with RH, describes noncritical zeros by harmonic measure, adapts time-frequency projectors at Archimedean places, and recovers the average zero count as a spectral deficit.

section_argument_map.label: General remarks
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Clarifies quotient-space, class-field, absorption-sign, arithmetic-site, and possible GL(n) extensions and limits.

section_argument_map.label: Appendix I. Proof of Theorem 1
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Develops homogeneous adelic distributions, Poisson summation, rapid decay, Sobolev approximate units, and the cokernel-orthogonal calculation that turns zeros and their multiplicities into spectrum and Jordan structure.

section_argument_map.label: Appendix II. Explicit formulas
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Rewrites Weil's explicit formula in the paper's test-function notation, compares local principal values under Fourier normalization, and proves the stated global explicit formula.

section_argument_map.label: Appendix III. Distribution trace formulas
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Gives the coordinate-free density, wave-front, pullback, kernel, and transversality foundations for the flow trace formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A longer mollifier becomes possible by combining three previously separate analytic inputs
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The introduction identifies the exact causal novelty: mean-square reduction, arithmetic main-term evaluation, and averaged Kloosterman control together permit mollifier length T^(4/7), beyond Levinson's T^(1/2).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A polynomial-weighted Möbius mollifier and flexible differential combination create optimization freedom
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source contrasts Levinson's fixed coefficients with polynomial mollifier weights and a more general combination of xi derivatives, deferring the final choices until a variational optimization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The method yields distinct lower bounds for critical-line and simple critical-line zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source separates the proportion of all critical-line zeros from the proportion that are simple and states the 0.4077 and 0.401 bounds, with the latter giving more than two fifths simple.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical-line zero counting is reduced to zeros of a mollified differential combination
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reality parity of xi derivatives turns zeta zeros into sign changes of the real part of eta; the argument principle and Littlewood's lemma then bound missing changes through the mean square of a shifted mollified approximation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A linear differential choice converts surviving sign changes into simple zeta zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The argument distinguishes zeros of the auxiliary real part from zeros of eta itself; under a specialized coefficient condition, the former imply a zeta zero while the latter exclusion guarantees nonvanishing derivative and hence simplicity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The mollified mean square becomes a quadratic functional minimized by an Euler-Lagrange equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 2 supplies the asymptotic for mollifiers shorter than T^(4/7); its main term is organized into a quadratic functional of P, whose boundary-constrained Euler-Lagrange solution gives the optimized numerical proportions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A two-shift local mean proposition generates the required differentiated global mean
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof packages the mollified zeta pair into a function analytic in two small shifts, applies a uniform asymptotic, and uses Cauchy's formula to recover the differential polynomial V and hence Theorem 2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: GCD factorization and a shift-reversal identity collapse the mollifier coefficient sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The first lemma changes summation order by the common divisor and evaluates the separated sums using earlier arithmetic lemmas; a second symmetry identity converts the paired shifts into the proposition's concise main term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Estermann functional equations and contour residues isolate the mollified mean's diagonal main term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An additive divisor Dirichlet series is analytically continued and functionally transformed; Mellin inversion and contour displacement split the result into main, remainder, and error pieces, with a local residue lemma evaluating the main contribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dyadic decomposition reduces all off-diagonal errors to one averaged Kloosterman bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rapidly decaying remainder terms are discarded, the surviving error is organized by gcd and dyadic ranges, and Lemmas 7-8 convert kernel decay plus an arithmetic exponential-sum estimate into the threshold theta<4/7.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Vaughan's identity creates bilinear forms matched to averaged and individual Kloosterman estimates
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separating the gcd-dependent weights and decomposing Möbius coefficients produces three bilinear sums; medium ranges use the Deshouillers-Iwaniec averaged bound, while short ranges use Weil's bound, and the resulting exponent checks close Lemma 8.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The explicit formula turns zero locations into prime-counting error terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the Euler product, functional equation, critical strip, and explicit formula to show why the real parts of zeta zeros determine the scale of oscillation in weighted prime counts and why excluding zeros on the one-line proves the prime number theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Möbius cancellation reformulates RH but the natural square-root strengthening is false
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the Dirichlet series for reciprocal zeta and partial summation to equate RH with near-square-root cancellation of the Mertens sum, then distinguishes that epsilon-weakened criterion from Mertens's stronger disproved bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Several strong kinds of evidence still stop short of RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates finite verification, near-line density, positive proportions on the line, derivative-zero results, probabilistic Möbius heuristics, and aesthetic prime regularity, including a failed attempted converse to Rolle's theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hilbert–Pólya would prove RH by making ordinates eigenvalues of a Hermitian operator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compresses RH into a representation problem: find a natural self-adjoint operator whose real spectrum is exactly the nontrivial zero ordinates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pólya's route seeks a real-zero-preserving class for the Fourier transform of xi
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the even real critical-line xi function, its explicit Fourier transform, positivity, and de Bruijn's sufficient class to turn RH into membership in a structural family of entire Fourier transforms with only real zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Nyman–Beurling turns RH into density of fractional-part functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reframes RH as completeness in L2(0,1), then as vanishing best-approximation error by Dirichlet polynomials on the critical line and relates the conjectured convergence constant to zero multiplicities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit-formula duality becomes Weil and Li positivity criteria
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States Weil's prime-zero trace identity and the equivalence of RH with positivity for autocorrelation test functions, then reduces it to Li's explicit sequence of nonnegative coefficients while noting that a geometric interpretation making positivity transparent is missing.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH admits arithmetic, determinant, and divisor-sum tests far from its original language
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records Hardy–Littlewood's reciprocal-zeta series condition, Redheffer's divisibility-matrix determinant bound, and Lagarias's elementary divisor-sum inequality as exact equivalent criteria.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Spurious Selberg eigenvalues expose a spectral false friend
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that computed Laplace eigenvalues apparently matching zeta and Dirichlet-L zero ordinates arose from pseudo cusp forms and the numerical method; a legitimate match would have proved RH, so the episode demonstrates why numerical spectral coincidence is not an operator identification.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler products and functional equations organize a common RH class
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Moves from Dirichlet L-functions through number fields, modular forms, and elliptic curves to the Langlands program and Selberg's axioms, identifying structural conditions expected of any function satisfying an RH analogue.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pair correlation transfers a zero-spacing question to random Hermitian spectra
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains Montgomery's normalized pair-correlation conjecture, Dyson's identification with GUE eigenvalues, the extension to all local statistics, and Odlyzko's large-height computational confirmation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Characteristic-polynomial moments predict the missing constants in zeta moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses exact Haar averages of unitary characteristic polynomials to supply the previously unexplained combinatorial factors in all even moments of zeta, including agreement with independently conjectured low moments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Families of L-functions select unitary, symplectic, or orthogonal statistics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains Katz–Sarnak's identification of family monodromy with random-matrix symmetry types, why Haar measure is the correct ensemble, and how the model predicts low-zero, moment, value, and central-vanishing distributions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A hypothetical exceptional zero forces repulsion and class-number growth elsewhere
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects quadratic class numbers to L-values, traces Deuring–Heilbronn and Siegel arguments, and explains how a real zero near one makes a character mimic Möbius while repelling zeros of other L-functions, yielding strong but ineffective consequences.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Three routes hit sharp thresholds just before eliminating the exceptional zero
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares the Brun–Titchmarsh constant-two barrier, the inability of zero-spacing methods to cross half the average gap, and the exact fifty-percent nonvanishing ceiling for modular L-functions, each of which would solve the same exceptional-zero obstruction if improved slightly.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Forced multiple central zeros convert exotic L-functions into effective arithmetic bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains Goldfeld's observation that higher-order central vanishing yields an effective class-number lower bound, Gross–Zagier's realization of triple zeros, and the strategic turn toward high-rank elliptic-curve L-functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Iwaniec proposes approximating Möbius with coefficients from a forced-vanishing family
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a family of elliptic curves engineered to have a multiple central zero so that linear combinations of its L-function coefficients tame Möbius, reducing exceptional-zero control to a family moment bound and square-root cancellation in an incomplete exponential sum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Irregular L-function zeros motivate arithmetic families rather than classical differential equations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts regularly spaced zeros of classical ODE special functions with random-matrix-like and high-multiplicity L-function zeros, then argues that progress likely needs new families, moment theorems, modularity, arithmetic-geometric exponential-sum bounds, and systematic examples.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Supported kernels turn pair correlation into simplicity and non-average gap bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Specific sinc kernels bound the multiplicity-weighted diagonal and show a positive proportion of simple zeros, while a compactly supported gap kernel forces neighboring gaps below a computable fraction of the mean.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The large-frequency conjecture selects the complex Hermitian/unitary pair-correlation law

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The unitary analogy predicts determinants for k-tuples and extreme gaps, but low-zero numerics may converge slowly

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Subtracting reflected logarithmic derivatives yields a smoothed equality between zeros and prime powers

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The zero-side L2 norm is exactly the pair-correlation transform

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Diagonal Parseval estimates prove the transform only while prime-polynomial errors remain subordinate

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A nonnegative trigonometric polynomial controls the width of a classical zero-free region
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Historical improvements all use coefficientwise nonnegative, globally nonnegative cosine polynomials with a1>a0; Landau's ratio turns their shape into an asymptotic R0 bound, making polynomial design a mathematical optimization interface.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A hypothetical near-one zero is squeezed by a kernel inequality and a fixed-point update
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Kadiri's method assumes a zero just beyond a known region, builds height- and kernel-dependent parameters satisfying positivity constraints, derives an upper bound for the improved constant, then feeds each improvement back as the next known region until stable.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Splitting the height parameter prevents a favorable error term from being discarded
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A secondary eta threshold gives two denominator lower bounds, one from monotonicity and one retaining the nonpositive error C; balancing them by binary search yields most of the improvement over Kadiri, with updated verified height supplying the remainder.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Four error channels are bounded with sign-aware Taylor and gamma estimates
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Decomposing C into four summands allows independent treatment of coefficient/gamma terms, and a cubic exponential bound with directed rounding sharpens an integral majorant while preserving rigor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Direct low-zero data plus Lehman's formula replaces a generic zero-count error estimate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For zero height the total reciprocal-square sum minus verified zeros gives a tight remainder; at positive shifts a monotone test function in Lehman's explicit zero-sum estimate controls both tails beyond the exclusion window.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Splitting around the kernel peak makes the last gamma integral computably bounded
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The final error integral is partitioned where different explicit bounds apply and again around its shifted singular peak; analytic outer-tail estimates plus numerical compact integrals give a practical rigorous bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Squaring an exponential polynomial enforces global nonnegativity during annealing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Parameterizing f as the squared modulus of a finite exponential sum converts global positivity into construction, leaves coefficient nonnegativity and a1>a0 as cheap tests, and permits O(n) incremental autocorrelation updates under simulated annealing.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Optimizing Landau's constant and optimizing the finite zero-free constant select different polynomials
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Degree-40 searches improve the asymptotic Landau bound, but Kadiri evaluation favors smaller degree; retesting many near-optimal surrogate candidates and locally refining the true objective produces the degree-16 polynomial used for the best R0.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Increasing verified RH height gives diminishing zero-free-region returns
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Re-running the same method over many hypothetical verified heights yields an empirical inverse-log approach to a limiting constant, diagnosing polynomial and analytic structure rather than verified height as the eventual bottleneck.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A wider zero-free strip sharpens explicit prime-number-theorem errors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The new constant is inserted into an offset logarithmic zero-free region and then into established contour arguments, improving explicit bounds for theta, psi, and pi minus li and identifying further applications that inherit the change.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH gives the sharp logarithmic order for every fixed zeta moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The theorem reaches T(log T)^{k^2} for all fixed k, separates known low moments and lower bounds from the new range, and frames the advance over Soundararajan's epsilon-loss estimate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime blocks behave like independent Gaussian increments with decreasing later variance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Euler-product heuristic models log|zeta| by independent prime phases, identifies variance one half log log T, and observes that splitting primes into ranges creates nearly independent increments whose later blocks have smaller typical size.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Multiscale truncation and direct moments bypass two losses in large-value counting
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source isolates the length-versus-available-moments tradeoff and the loss from Markov tail bounds, then replaces them with block-dependent truncation powers, first-bad exceptional sets, and direct integration of truncated exponential products.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A tunable RH majorant bounds log|zeta| by primes and prime squares
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Soundararajan's majorant permits a freely chosen polynomial length and keeps the zero contribution one-sided, while the accompanying cosine mean-value proposition supplies the orthogonality needed to integrate its powers.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Cosine products have a main term exactly when every prime multiplicity pairs
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proposition 2 makes the random-phase analogy rigorous for bounded products: odd prime multiplicities vanish from the main term, even ones factor multiplicatively, and distinct primes do not interact.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Good and first-bad sets turn one long polynomial into a controlled multiscale partition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Geometrically growing prime ranges define good points where every block is small and exceptional strata indexed by the first uncontrolled block; three lemmas then separately bound the good integral, bad strata, and prime-square addition before their estimates are summed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positivity and square support turn truncated block exponentials into the Gaussian moment scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: On the good set each exponential series is truncated at a block-specific degree, squared to preserve positivity when extending the integration domain, expanded through Proposition 2, and reassembled using multiplicativity; square support then yields exp(k^2 sum 1/p), hence the sharp logarithmic order.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A first oversized block pays for itself through a high even power
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: On S(j), the first failing block is inserted at a high even power while earlier blocks remain truncatable; orthogonality then yields an exponential penalty in beta_{j+1}^{-1} log(1/beta_{j+1}) strong enough to sum over all failure levels.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dyadic exceptional sets keep the prime-square polynomial from spoiling the sharp moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The prime-square contribution is split into dyadic prime ranges, typical ranges sum to O(1), and a first atypical range is penalized by a very high moment on a disjoint prime set, preserving the main log^{k^2} scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The multiscale method transfers when a family supplies a polynomial majorant and square orthogonality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under GRH, quadratic-character central values have a prime majorant with a deterministic prime-square shift, while family averaging kills nonsquare products; analogous good/bad strata then give the conjecturally sharp X(log X)^{k(k+1)/2} upper bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The rigorous short-polynomial constraint explains the poor constant, while Gaussian optimization predicts the random-matrix scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Tracking constants identifies the need to choose beta_I exponentially small in k as the source of a doubly exponential loss; allowing a conjecturally longer Gaussian prime polynomial and optimizing its length recovers an exp(-k^2 log k+O(k^2)) factor close to random matrix theory.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The functional-equation phase parametrizes intersections of zeta with every line through the origin
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Because Delta has unit modulus on the critical line, roots of a phase equation identify exactly the nonzero zeta values lying on a chosen direction, separating phase roots from zeta zeros in the counting function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Phase intersections have T log T density and explicit first and second directional moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorems 1 and 2 jointly quantify how often each direction is hit and how the directional values average, with the second leading term independent of direction and the first sensitive to phase.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Directional moments imply conditional means and unconditional large values on prescribed half-lines
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper derives the geometric mean circle under RH, explains the positive-real bias, and proves arbitrarily large real and direction-constrained critical-line values from moment growth.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Clockwise phase winding gives the asymptotic count of directional intersections
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A logarithmic-derivative asymptotic shows monotone accelerating rotation of Delta; integrating the winding number yields the count, with endpoint adjustment contributing only logarithmic error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A logarithmic derivative of the phase equation converts the first discrete moment into contour integrals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The residue method isolates phase roots, uses the functional equation to move the main contour, expands a rapidly convergent geometric factor, and applies Gonek's lemma to extract the first-moment main term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The same contour mechanism plus the divisor problem yields the second directional moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replacing zeta by the product zeta(s)zeta(1-s) preserves the contour architecture while the inner Dirichlet convolution introduces the classical divisor-sum asymptotic and its logarithmic-square main term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Counting plus second moments force large values, while the first moment fixes their sign balance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Normalizing by the intersection count gives directional means; comparing the second moment with a hypothetical uniform cap forces square-root-log large values, and Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the number of nonzero phase intersections.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Directional moment formulas translate into moment bounds for Hardy's Z at Gram points
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The phi-zero specialization relates failures of Gram's law to negative real zeta values, recovers first and second Z moments, and uses Cauchy-Schwarz to prove a fourth-moment lower bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The circle of directional means summarizes the positive-real bias but higher-degree transfer is obstructed
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Averaging directional means yields one-half and motivates a heuristic split between small and large values, while the authors distinguish easy Dirichlet-L transfer from the harder higher-degree setting.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler's product turns unique factorization into a zero-free half-plane and Riemann continues beyond it
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains how absolute convergence and unique factorization identify the Dirichlet series with the prime Euler product, why this excludes zeros for real part greater than one, and why contour continuation is needed to reach the rest of the plane.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Möbius inversion and zeta zeros reconstruct the prime staircase
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the weighted prime-power counter J, inverts it to pi, replaces J by a sum over zeros, handles logarithmic branches, and uses the functional equation to explain trivial zeros and the quartet symmetry of nontrivial zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The explicit zero sum requires symmetric ordering to encode a discontinuous arithmetic object
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts a rapidly convergent smooth main term with the conditionally convergent zero correction, explains the mandated conjugate/increasing-height order, and interprets collective oscillations as forming the prime staircase.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical-line symmetry turns the explicit formula into waves and the zero-free boundary yields PNT
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States RH, pairs zeros under RH to obtain cosine/sine fluctuations around the main trend, and explains why merely excluding zeros from real part one already makes the main term dominate enough for the Prime Number Theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero verification and density results accumulate evidence without closing the universal claim
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Distinguishes finite computation at many heights, zero-count asymptotics, and positive-proportion critical-line theorems from RH, then contrasts the Euler and Hadamard products as prime-side and zero-side factorizations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH appears both as a prime-counting error threshold and as the zero time of a real-zero heat flow
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Pairs the von Koch/Schoenfeld prime-error equivalence with the de Bruijn-Newman deformation, where a monotone real-zero property compresses RH into the sign of one transition constant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integral equalities and divisor-sum inequalities encode RH with very different falsification interfaces
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Places Volchkov-type integral criteria beside Lagarias and Robin inequalities, showing that equivalent statements can expose either global analytic cancellation or a single integer counterexample while remaining computationally delicate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hilbert-Polya would replace a location theorem by self-adjoint spectral reality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains the proposed mechanism: identify zero ordinates as eigenvalues of a Hermitian physical problem so their reality forces critical-line location.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Montgomery pair correlation and GUE universality constrain the hidden spectral system
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects zero repulsion to Hermitian random-matrix eigenvalue repulsion, defines unfolding, distinguishes symmetry universality classes, and reports how high-zero computations support the GUE rather than Poisson/GOE/GSE model.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The xp counting law matches the zero staircase but fails the operator requirements
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lists the desired Hermitian chaotic system, motivates H=xp by its matching leading counting law, and then records fatal issues: special regularization, disagreement of lower terms, continuous spectrum, and integrability.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Characteristic-polynomial moments supply the missing constants in zeta moment conjectures
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Moves from known second and fourth moments to the Keating-Snaith GUE characteristic-polynomial theorem and shows how its universal factor combines with an arithmetic Euler product to predict all fixed moments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Spectral realization alone is underdetermined, and proposed operators relocate rather than remove RH's difficulty
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Notes that many integrable Hamiltonians can realize any suitably growing spectrum, then explains how Connes's trace formula and Okubo's boundary condition leave an equally hard completeness/normalizability problem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Trivial zeta zeros are realized by a shifted inverted oscillator operator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the harmonic-oscillator eigenproblem to construct an explicit differential operator whose eigenvalues are the evenly spaced trivial zeros, providing a controlled contrast with the nontrivial-zero problem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quantum verification proposals still require an independently sufficient RH criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Distinguishes encoding assumed critical-line zeros in a unitary circuit from a verifying computation, and criticizes quantum prime-counting against Schoenfeld's bound as an artificial acceleration rather than a new proof mechanism.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic integer energies make the canonical partition function equal zeta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses prime-labeled one-particle states, unique factorization, and additive logarithmic energy to construct composite states whose Boltzmann sum is the zeta Dirichlet series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional-equation duality suggests a circle theorem, but the zeta spin model lies outside the proven class
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares zeta's functional equation with Kramers-Wannier duality, maps the critical line to the unit circle, and outlines a Lee-Yang route before identifying that Knauf's zeta-ratio spin interaction does not satisfy the hypotheses of available circle theorems.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Random-walk intuition motivates Mertens, but the strong bound fails while an epsilon-weakened form remains equivalent to RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Interprets Möbius signs as walk increments, derives boundedness of 1/zeta to the right of one-half from the Mertens bound, records its computational disproof, and states the weaker Littlewood equivalence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Möbius-weighted long-range walk can locate a strip without excluding off-line zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines a jump law involving Möbius values and explains that general probability constraints recover some strip information yet remain compatible with zeros off the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Open-billiard escape asymptotics translate RH into a measurable survival limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates circular-billiard survival probability to zeta, states an RH-equivalent double limit, and identifies how a slower-than-square-root small-hole law could experimentally refute RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A shaped disc physically implements a Fourier representation of zeta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains how van der Pol encoded the kernel of an integral representation on a paper disc, optically sampled it, and superposed frequencies to locate critical-line zeros by an analog Fourier transform.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Electrostatic fields and quasicrystals offer geometric encodings without a completeness theorem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts an electrostatic vector-field formula for large critical-line zeros with the proposal that all zero locations form a one-dimensional quasicrystal whose missing classification might constrain them.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Vertical shifts of zeta approximate any nonvanishing analytic target locally
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States Voronin universality and uses self-approximation to motivate a fractal interpretation, a striking counterpoint to seeking a single simple global shape.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reconstructing zeros as a spectrum and iterating Newton's map generate different fractal structures
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reports an inverse spectral potential with zeta zeros as eigenvalues and contrasts it with Newton-basin iteration, which visualizes attraction to infinitely many zeta zeros from varying initial points.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite confirmation can coexist with remote counterexamples
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the eventual sign change of pi-Li and the false Mertens conjecture to show why enormous verified ranges cannot exclude a remote off-line zeta zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reviews the exact and asymptotic zero counts, isolates the fluctuating argument term, and repeatedly distinguishes an equation intended to locate one labeled critical-line zero from formulas that count zeros over the full strip.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Select a symmetric phase branch to enumerate critical-line zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Factors the completed zeta function into magnitude and phase, uses functional-equation symmetry, regularizes the zeta argument from the right, and selects theta equals reflected theta with cosine zero to derive an n-indexed asymptotic equation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Turn unique labeled solutions into equality of critical-line and whole-strip counts
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the integer label and phase jump to construct N0(T), observes that its displayed asymptotic matches the whole-strip count, and infers no room for additional zeros only under well-definedness and uniqueness of every labeled solution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Replace Stirling's phase by theta and expose uniqueness as the RH hinge
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the exact theta-plus-arg-zeta equation, explains how a positive delta gives upward phase jumps, and states explicitly that uniqueness for every n would make its exact count equal the whole-strip count and hence prove RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Define cosine zero at a smoothed sign discontinuity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Interprets the selected phase condition as assigning zero to a discontinuous normalized real completed-zeta sign and argues that symmetric extraneous factors are canceled from the construction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arg-zeta is both the informative fluctuation and the numerical discontinuity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why the phase equation is claimed to be stronger than counting or the raw equation zeta equals zero, responds to circularity, and shows that positive-delta smoothing is needed for the staircase that counts known line zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Drop the oscillatory phase and invert the smooth zero equation with Lambert W
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transforms the average transcendental equation into Lambert W to obtain an explicit n-only approximation, identifies its large-n spacing, and distinguishes the result from Gram points and Gram-law bracketing.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Let the phase jump displace the smooth initializer onto a known zero
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how the arg-zeta fluctuation corrects Lambert-W estimates, brackets the sign change with Brent's method, and compares solutions across scales and precisions with independently tabulated zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The oscillatory phase is necessary to reproduce GUE pair correlation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines normalized local spacings and an Odlyzko-style windowed pair-correlation statistic, then reports that phase-corrected numerical solutions reproduce it while the smooth Lambert-W approximation does not.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Phase-corrected approximate zeros sharpen the explicit prime-counting formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reviews Riemann's explicit formula and Moebius inversion, then compares prime-count reconstructions using smooth versus phase-corrected zero approximations to show the informational role of arg zeta.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Decrease the phase regularizer around successive exact-equation roots
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Provides a concrete iterative scheme initialized by Lambert W, with positive delta reduced at each root solve, and reports recovery of known Gram-law-failure and high-precision zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Saturation remains conditional and the authors disclaim a rigorous proof
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Collects the exact logical status in one place: existence of the stated on-line family, asserted smoothing and uniqueness, conditional count saturation, numerical reproduction of statistics, and the explicit statement that the approach is not a rigorous proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler product and functional symmetry constrain the zero geometry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates the Dirichlet series to a product over primes, analytically continues it, and uses the functional equation and Gamma poles to distinguish trivial zeros, the critical strip, and symmetry about the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime counting is a smooth term corrected by nontrivial zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States RH and the PNT boundary criterion, then presents the explicit formula in which zero terms refine the logarithmic-integral approximation to prime counting.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The zeta-zero density splits into a smooth count and prime-power oscillations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Decomposes zero density into an average logarithmic term and an oscillatory sum indexed by primes and repetitions, then changes variables so zero counts and chaotic periodic-orbit counts share exponential growth.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integrability confines trajectories to tori while billiard geometry can create chaos
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains action-angle solvability, the dimensional obstruction to autonomous one-dimensional chaos, and how billiard boundary geometry changes periodicity, mixing, and escape behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Open-billiard escape corrections encode totients, Moebius sums, and zeta zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Classifies long-lived periodic trajectories by coprime pairs, converts their sums to Euler-totient and Ramanujan-Moebius terms, Mellin transforms the escape probability, and states RH-equivalent second-order asymptotics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A flow trace turns global evolution spectrum into periodic-orbit data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expresses the evolution-operator trace as a sum over primitive periodic orbits and repetitions weighted by monodromy determinants, establishing the classical precursor of quantum trace formulas.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gutzwiller replaces invariant-torus quantization by an unstable-orbit expansion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates smooth Thomas-Fermi density from orbit-dependent oscillations and presents Gutzwiller's Green-function trace as a quantization route when Bohr-Sommerfeld action variables are unavailable.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Matching trace formulas predicts the qualitative Riemann dynamics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Maps primes to primitive orbits, logarithms of primes to periods, and prime powers to stability factors, then infers scale invariance, instability, broken time reversal, and quasi-one-dimensionality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hilbert-Polya turns RH into self-adjoint spectral reality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains that realizing nontrivial zeros as eigenvalues of a self-adjoint Hamiltonian would force their ordinates to be real and separates scattering-state from bound-state model families.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Negative curvature yields an exact Selberg orbit expansion and zeta scattering poles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects compact negative-curvature chaos to an exact density-of-states trace formula and, for a noncompact surface, places zeta factors and nontrivial zeros in the scattering matrix.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Jost and phase-shift analogies realize zero data but do not explain RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Maps Jost zeros to the critical line, surveys coupling-constant and redundant-pole constructions, and compares the phase of zeta with scattering Argand diagrams.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Inverted oscillators and xp recover separate zeta components but boundary conditions remain decisive
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows an inverted oscillator reproducing the oscillatory zeta phase, while a regularized xp Hamiltonian reproduces the smooth zero count and satisfies several predicted symmetries; dilation and canonical-exchange ideas expose the unresolved boundary/compactification problem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Smooth zero counts invert to smooth potentials, but exact zeros force fractal structure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses Abel-type semiclassical inversion for the mean count, then compares variational, dressing, and inverse-scattering reconstructions of exact low zeros to separate method artifacts from long-range-correlation-driven fractality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The trace-formula sign suggests zeros are missing lines rather than emitted levels
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the negative oscillatory sign to motivate Connes's gap interpretation and contrasts highly correlated zeta zeros with nearly Poisson primes despite their explicit-formula interconversion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: GUE agreement fixes symmetry class but short orbits break universality at long range
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives Poisson spacing for uncorrelated spectra, identifies Montgomery's pair correlation with GUE, extends the comparison to higher correlations, and explains finite-height long-range deviations through system-specific shortest orbits.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arbitrary-spectrum Hamiltonians make naturality essential
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reports a nonconstructive theorem producing infinitely many integrable Hamiltonians for any bounded spectrum, including zeta zeros, showing that mere spectral realization is too weak without a natural mechanism.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lattice energy leads to Epstein zeta functions whose RH analogue can fail
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds Madelung energies from conditionally convergent lattice quadratic forms, represents them by Epstein zeta functions with functional symmetry, and records that suitable forms in every dimension violate the tempting generalized RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Thermal observables turn zeta analytic structure into density and phase-transition constraints
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses Moebius/Laplace inversion to recover phonon density from specific heat and interprets its admissible exponent strip as zero-free, while the Bose-gas particle integral uses zeta's sign and pole to exclude homogeneous condensation below three dimensions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Spectral-zeta poles separate thermodynamic limits from finite-size corrections
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Represents condensate fluctuations by a Mellin integral involving spectral and Riemann zeta functions, with leading poles controlling bulk behavior and next poles finite-size corrections, then translates a harmonic trap into an asymptotic partition statistic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Log-prime energies make the bosonic partition function exactly zeta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses unique factorization to biject bosonic occupation vectors with positive integers, so total energy is logarithmic and the canonical partition function is zeta; its pole becomes a Hagedorn temperature.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exclusion and Dirichlet convolution generate zeta ratios and particle transmutation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns Pauli exclusion into square-free state counting and a zeta(s)/zeta(2s) partition function, generalizes occupancy through parafermions, and uses twisted Dirichlet convolution to equate interacting boson mixing with decoupled fermion-boson gases.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A finite-temperature interaction argument reaches RH only by assuming its decisive nonvanishing behavior
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs energy-dependent scattering kernels and a quasiperiodic potential across the critical strip, then argues physical thermodynamic quantities forbid off-line zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Moebius random walk shows why vast numerical agreement can mislead
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Interprets the Mertens sum as a walk, recalls the square-root bound as sufficient for RH, and records its indirect disproof only at an enormous scale while explaining that this does not refute RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-factor counts become Gaussian through a Brownian-motion viewpoint
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines a factorization-driven walk and uses the Erdos-Kac limit theorem to show that the number of distinct prime factors has Gaussian fluctuations about log log N.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Pairs zeros under the functional equation, integrates a decaying rational test function against the zero-counting measure, and uses strict equality in a convexity comparison to make concentration on the critical line equivalent to a computable phase integral.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Li coefficients encode the Riemann Hypothesis
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The introduction states that positivity of a derivative-defined sequence is equivalent to RH and rewrites the same coefficients as a symmetrically interpreted sum over nontrivial zeros, establishing the two representations studied in the paper.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Separating the general inequality mechanism from zeta-specific arithmetic
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors contrast Li's use of zeta-integral positivity with their plan: first a criterion for arbitrary multisets, then an explicit-formula arithmetic expression and comparison with Weil's criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetric convergence makes multiset zero sums well defined
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper defines a multiplicity-aware symmetric limiting convention and gives summability hypotheses under which the transformed sums are absolutely or symmetrically convergent; conjugation invariance makes the limiting value real.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One-sided transformed sums characterize multiset containment in a half-plane
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The theorem equates half-plane containment with positivity and subexponential one-sided bounds for a sequence of transformed multiset sums. If containment fails, finitely many maximal-modulus offenders dominate and simultaneous Diophantine approximation aligns their phases, forcing exponentially large negative values infinitely often.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional-equation symmetry upgrades the half-plane test to a critical-line test
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For a multiset invariant under conjugation and reflection across the functional-equation center, applying the general theorem to the multiset and its reflection makes the transformed sums real and equates coefficient positivity with every element lying on the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Guinand self-reciprocity versus Weil arithmetic in explicit formulas
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source distinguishes an earlier self-reciprocal-transform viewpoint from Weil's arithmetic emphasis and explains why it restates the explicit formula in Mellin-transform language.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mellin test functions translate zero sums into prime and archimedean terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Regularity and decay conditions define a test-function class with an involution and Mellin transform; the explicit formula then represents a symmetric sum over zeros by arithmetic prime-power terms and continuous correction terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Li's transformed summand has a concrete inverse-Mellin test function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors identify an inverse Mellin transform supported on one side of the multiplicative identity and express it through an explicit polynomial, producing the test function later inserted into the explicit formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncating the Li test function exposes an arithmetic coefficient formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Because the raw inverse-Mellin function violates the decay hypothesis, the proof truncates it, applies the explicit formula to the admissible approximation, and sends the cutoff to zero after evaluating prime and continuous terms, yielding an arithmetic expression for the Li coefficients.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-number estimates justify removal of the test-function cutoff
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The remaining zero-side limit is controlled using the prime number theorem with error term and a classical zero-free region, which make the discarded contributions decay faster than any negative power of the logarithmic cutoff.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Li positivity is an explicit test-function slice of Weil positivity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Multiplicative convolution turns into product under Mellin transform; self-convolution therefore gives a transform positive on the critical line. A source-stated identity shows the Li test functions fit this pattern, so their positivity has Weil's meaning while requiring only a simple explicit family.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Stieltjes-type constants give a second route to the Li coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The arithmetic constants from the explicit-formula expression are compared with Stieltjes constants, related through generating-series expansions, and said to yield coefficient formulas directly after the same conformal change of variable, without invoking the explicit formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States RH-conditional upper and unconditional integer-moment lower bounds with the same product of min(1/|alpha_i-alpha_j|,log T), thereby locating the transition scale independently of the conjectured constant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unitary characteristic-polynomial correlation predicts the zeta regimes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses translation invariance to reduce two matrix arguments to their difference and the identification N approximately log(T/2pi) to formulate the three zeta regimes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Merged matrix shifts behave as one higher moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rescales all contour variables at 1/N when alpha N tends to zero, so the two pole sets coalesce and the joint moment becomes the ordinary moment of order 2k.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Separated matrix shifts factor after balanced pole assignment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Deforms each contour around two pole clusters and shows that only assignments with k variables in each cluster on both sides have maximal order, yielding a product of two ordinary moments times a separation factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite microscopic separation retains a sine-kernel determinant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: At alpha N tending to a finite nonzero constant, the scaled contour limit remains a nontrivial determinant continuous through coalescing arguments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integrate large-deviation level sets to bound shifted moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expresses the joint moment as an integral of the measure where a weighted sum of log absolute zeta values exceeds V, reducing the theorem to three tail regimes governed by one covariance parameter W.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Split the log-zeta majorant into short and long prime blocks
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under RH, majorizes each shifted log zeta by a weighted prime polynomial, discards higher prime powers, and partitions primes so either a short correlated block or a long rare block must be large.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A cosine prime sum truncates correlation at inverse shift distance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that the cross term between two shifted prime polynomials grows only like log min(1/|a|,log z), producing the pairwise correlation factor used throughout the paper.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-polynomial moments yield Gaussian then exponential tails
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies a mean-value lemma with optimized integer moments separately to the short and long blocks, obtaining the tail bounds needed by the level-set integral.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The resonator norm turns shift geometry into clustered zeta poles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands the short Dirichlet polynomial, factors its coefficient square into zeta functions at every pairwise shift difference, and uses a Perron contour whose poles encode which shifts are within 1/log T.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Enclose nearby poles together and suppress the far clusters
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Partitions shift pairs into microscopic and nonmicroscopic sets, replaces separate close residues by one small contour, and proves its main contribution has the product scale dictated by close and far differences.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Approximate the zeta product by a long exponentially smoothed series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Moves a Mellin contour, collects the zeta-product residue at zero, and bounds the functional poles and new line to approximate the product uniformly on the integration range.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A short resonator makes the diagonal dominate

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Row and column differences cancel the Vandermonde zero

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Graph positivity makes every far residue negligible

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines coefficients from reciprocal even zeta values, uses them to continue zeta, and states that RH is equivalent to ck decaying like k to minus three-fourths plus epsilon, with the sharper exponent tied to simple zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Splits ck into a trivial-zero trend of order k to minus two and a nontrivial-zero term whose k to minus three-fourths envelope is the RH-sensitive component.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pochhammer asymptotics turn the nontrivial-zero residue sum into a rapidly damped oscillatory series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites the zero contribution through gamma functions, pairs conjugate zeros, extracts the power of k, and under RH obtains exponential damping in zero height so the first zero dominates and truncated computation is fast.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Multiplying by k to the three-fourths turns RH into bounded oscillation and exposes the off-line exponent
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains how a critical-line bound becomes confinement to a fixed strip and sets up the simple-zero mechanism by which a real-part displacement changes the power of k.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Conditional logarithmic Hamiltonian creates opposite time directions

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands the zeta-state Wigner function, interprets logarithmic dispersion as a curling wedge with interference negativity, and identifies the phase-space overlap with the squared zeta autocorrelation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Entangled branches rotate oppositely while off-diagonal coherence does not rotate

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A multiplier both solves a divergence equation and is the velocity Hessian of a Lagrangian; ratios generate first integrals, symmetry determinants generate multipliers, and double integration exposes gauge-equivalent or inequivalent variational formulations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Linearization selects a maximal-Noether Lagrangian and a continuum-spectrum quantum equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Sierra classical equation has the maximal eight-dimensional Lie algebra, an abelian intransitive subalgebra maps it to a free particle, and the associated multiplier yields a Lagrangian whose five Noether symmetries determine the displayed Schroedinger equation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A different symmetry pair gives a different Lagrangian but again a freely parameterized continuum equation

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The original Hamiltonian Lagrangian has fewer symmetries and still yields a continuum PDE
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Lagrangian derived from Sierra's Hamiltonian admits only three Noether symmetries; preserving exactly these produces a parabolic equation reducible to an elementary time equation with arbitrary spatial functions, so using the Hamiltonian-compatible variational structure does not restore discreteness.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The cosh model is classically linearizable but has competing variational structures

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weak value distributions become smooth densities through Fourier decay
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Sets up finite Borel measures, weak convergence, parameter integration, Fourier uniqueness and inversion, and the hierarchy from integrable polynomially weighted transforms to smooth densities and from exponential transform decay to real analyticity or entire extension.
