result_and_mechanism_map.title: Completed Eisenstein series, continuation, and two symmetries
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates two series representations to meromorphic continuation, the s↦1−s functional equation, and modular invariance, supplying the structural symmetries used by every later integral.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier decomposition isolates an exceptional constant term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Decomposes the Eisenstein series into entire nonconstant coefficients built from divisor sums and K-Bessel functions versus a meromorphic constant term built from two completed-zeta terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Measures turn Eisenstein symmetry into an RH test family
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines F_mu as integration over the modular surface, explains inheritance of the functional equation, realizes Fourier coefficients through horocycle measures, and states the nonnegative-measure RH objective.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Semistable-lattice integral produces Weng's rank-two zeta function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects Mellin integration over semistable-lattice moduli to an Eisenstein integral, states its continuation and functional equation, and gives the rank-two RH theorem while noting the absence of an Euler product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncation converts geometric integration to a shifted zeta combination
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Horizontal integration deletes nonconstant Fourier modes, yielding an explicit two-term expression I(T,s); Theorem 2 gives its sharp T≥1 RH range and the T=1 partition identifies it with Weng's zeta function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why the constant Fourier coefficient is the difficult case
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains that nonconstant coefficients inherit imaginary-axis zeros from two factors, whereas the meromorphic constant coefficient requires a modified RH and Maass-Selberg input.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exact exceptional-zero bifurcation for the constant term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 3 identifies the cutoff y*=4πe^{-γ}, distinguishes the no-exception and two-real-zero regimes, describes monotone escape toward 1, and contrasts this behavior with Epstein zeta functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two proof mechanisms and a polynomially weighted extension
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the Hadamard block-inequality route from the Maass-Selberg route and records a less elegant numerical extension that bounds off-line zeros for polynomially weighted combinations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Distinct routes to line-zero results for Eisenstein-derived functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Maps Taylor's differencing result, Vinogradov-Takhtajan heuristics, Zagier's representation at zeta zeros, Ki's finite Fourier truncations, and three proof approaches to Theorem 3.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A zero-strip hypothesis forces shifted sums to vanish on one line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 4 abstracts the core mechanism: an entire genus-zero/one function with real and functional-equation symmetries and a bounded zero strip yields a strict shifted-modulus inequality and line zeros for every phased sum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetry blocks remove Hadamard convergence factors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Partitions zeros into functional-equation/conjugation orbits, proves block convergence from the strip bound, removes exponential factors, and uses the functional equation to force the remaining linear exponential to vanish.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pairing rho with 1−conjugate(rho) creates a half-plane modulus separator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reduces the shifted-function ratio to independent zero-block factors and shows each paired distance ratio lies strictly above or below one according to the side of the critical line, excluding zeros off it.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: What survives without real-axis symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies constant modulus on the critical line as sufficient for the local pairing argument, explains why global Hadamard blocks then need extra hypotheses, and indicates the extension to general automorphic L-functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Scaled xi shifts prove the truncation-integral RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Chooses F(s)=xi(2s−1/2) so the known critical-strip containment matches c=1/4, converts I(T,s) to an entire antisymmetric H(T,s), and uses T≥1 to amplify the strict ratio beyond one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An antisymmetric entire transform makes both constant-term summands entire
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why the natural entire multiple G is replaced by H with an extra central zero: the alternative representation makes both summands entire and separates the proof into nonreal and real-zero problems.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Maass-Selberg positivity excludes nonreal off-line zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: At a zero of the constant term, reflection kills the boundary side of the Maass-Selberg relation while the integral side cannot vanish off the relevant symmetry lines, forcing every nonreal zero onto the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positivity confines real constant-term zeros to (0,1)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses positivity of the Eisenstein series and the horocycle-average identity to exclude real zeros above 1, then reflects the conclusion below 0 by the functional equation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Real zeros become a positive scalar level-set equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites H(y,σ)=0 as F(y,σ)=y^{2σ−1}f(σ)=1 and obtains positivity of f from the symmetry-grouped xi product, reducing zero location to one-variable shape analysis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The central derivative determines the exceptional-zero threshold
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Differentiates the scalar level-set function, shows the central derivative changes sign once, and evaluates the unique transition parameter through xi'(0)/xi(0) as 4πe^{-γ}.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-block derivatives enforce unimodality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Differentiates −f'/f into an elementary term and blockwise xi logarithmic derivatives, then uses the known height of xi zeros to make every derivative contribution positive on (1/2,1).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unimodality yields zero-free and two-exception regimes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the monotone logarithmic derivative to show F decreases below the threshold and has a single interior return to level one above it, producing exactly one real zero on each side by symmetry and motion toward the poles.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Simplicity, zero density, and monotone motion for I(T,s)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States that all truncation-integral zeros are simple, gives their count as the xi count plus a parameter-dependent linear term, and asserts strictly decreasing positive ordinates as T grows.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical-line zeros become phase crossings of xi
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Represents H(T,1/2+it) as a sine of θ(2t)+t log T, turning zeros into phase congruences, and imports a differenced-xi theorem to establish the T=1 simple-zero base case.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Phase monotonicity controls simplicity, count, and parameter motion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Adds log T to the phase derivative, invokes nonnegative xi phase rotation, derives simple crossings and the asymptotic count, then reads decreasing zero ordinates directly from monotonicity in both variables.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A wrong-way phase contribution obstructs monotone zero motion for a0
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gives the analogous zero count, identifies the multiple-zero migration to the real axis, and explains why a factor whose argument turns oppositely prevents the I(T,s) monotonicity proof from transferring directly.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Direct verification leaves the Fourier-coefficient RH mechanism unexplained
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates proof of a line-zero property from conceptual explanation, asks why the constant term needs y≥1 and admits exceptional zeros, and proposes truncation as a representation in which the zero-th coefficient regains RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integrated Fourier coefficients reduce to an integrated K-Bessel zero problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines twisted hyperbolic integrals J_n and isolates a special-function condition whose imaginary-axis zeros would imply RH for the whole family.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Laplacian structure kills only the zero-mode full-surface integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts Zagier's identically vanishing K_0, explained by a Laplacian eigenfunction property, with potentially nontrivial full-surface integrals for other Fourier modes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Smooth parameterized zeros are predicted not to exhibit GUE spacing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Makes a falsifiable zero-statistics prediction from the behavior of related differenced L-functions, explicitly contrasting it with a tempting random-matrix analogy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Averaging Epstein zeta functions sharpens an approximate real-zero cutoff
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates the nearly identical Bateman-Grosswald threshold for individual Epstein zeta functions to the exact cutoff for their x-average, the Eisenstein constant term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sublattice covolumes form a canonical convex polygon
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines lattice covolume, rankwise minimal slopes, and the convex envelope controlled by the sublattice intersection/sum inequality, creating the representation used to define stability.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Canonical polygon vertices induce a unique filtration and stability test
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains increasing-slope canonical vertices, their unique nested sublattices, the Harder-Narasimhan analogy, and the stable/semistable/unstable distinctions with an example.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rank-two semistability becomes the geometric region D_ss
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Quotients lattice bases by integer changes, rotations, and homotheties, identifies rank-two lattices with the modular upper half-plane, and converts the canonical-polygon test into y≤1 in the fundamental domain.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weng's lattice zeta specializes to the Eisenstein integral at rank two
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expresses the rank-r zeta as integration of Epstein zeta sums over determinant-one semistable lattices and identifies the rank-two inner sum and domain with the paper's Eisenstein-series construction.

section_argument_map.label: 2. Proof of Theorem 2

section_argument_map.label: 3. Proof of Theorem 3
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses Maass-Selberg exclusion of nonreal off-line zeros and a real-variable monotonicity analysis to locate the exceptional real-zero bifurcation.

section_argument_map.label: 4. Distribution of Zeros

section_argument_map.label: 5. Concluding Remarks
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: States conceptual gaps, proposes related integrals and special-function reductions, and contrasts predicted zero statistics and Epstein-zero thresholds.

section_argument_map.label: 6. Appendix: Stable and semi-stable lattices

source_identity.title: The Riemann hypothesis for certain integrals of Eisenstein series

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Horocycle/truncation integration selects the constant Fourier mode, the resulting two shifted completed-zeta terms admit a symmetry-blocked product comparison, and T≥1 turns that comparison into a strict half-plane modulus barrier.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: This mechanism proves RH only for the specified integrated/truncated combinations; it neither proves RH for zeta itself nor conceptually explains every Eisenstein coefficient.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: From Fourier projection to a shifted-xi modulus barrier

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Canonical-polygon semistability selects D_ss in rank two, Weng's lattice Mellin integral becomes an Eisenstein integral over that region, and the fundamental-domain partition converts it to the T=1 truncation integral whose zeros are controlled by Theorem 2.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The rank-two identification does not extend the proved RH result to Weng's higher-rank zeta functions, which have different groups and no asserted Euler product.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Semistability geometry identifies Weng's rank-two zeta with the T=1 theorem

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Maass-Selberg first confines nonreal zeros to the critical line; positivity and symmetry isolate real zeros in (0,1); the scalar level-set representation then turns the central derivative sign at y* and strict log-derivative monotonicity into creation of one symmetric exceptional pair.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The proof is specific to this completed-zeta combination and depends on delicate formula-level inequalities; the Landau-Siegel language is analogy, not identity of arithmetic mechanism.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Exceptional zeros as a one-parameter level-set bifurcation

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Writing critical-line values as a sine of a rotating xi phase unifies zero detection, simplicity, an asymptotic counting correction, and monotone motion under T; the failed transfer to a0 pinpoints an oppositely rotating factor and the real-zero escape.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: For a0 the analogous motion and simplicity statements are partly conjectural/numerical and need additional analytic estimates.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Phase rotation links zero density, simplicity, and motion

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The paper itself separates several successful direct verification technologies from the unresolved question of why Eisenstein Fourier coefficients should display RH behavior, then proposes truncation, integrated Bessel functions, full-surface modes, and zero-motion statistics as tests of possible mechanisms.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: These proposals are not established unifications; some are conditional or heuristic and must not be promoted to proved explanations.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Direct line-zero verification versus a conceptual Eisenstein mechanism

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Derivative zero counts reformulate RH and reveal concentration near one-half
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the approximate equality between zeta and zeta-prime zero counts, the Speiser equivalence, clustering of kth-derivative zeros, signed first-moment identities, one-sided short-interval bounds, and inheritance under further differentiation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A sign-controlled logarithmic derivative equates zeta and derivative zero counts
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Pairs zeros under the functional equation, expresses the real logarithmic derivative as a boundary-sign sum, indents around critical-line zeros, and uses zero change of argument of zeta-prime/zeta to obtain equal counts up to O(log T), with an alternative forcing many left zeros if no good horizontal sequence exists.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rolle interlacing and argument variation classify derivative zeros left of zero
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the functional-equation logarithmic derivative with Rolle's theorem between trivial zeros and boundary argument change to show exactly one real zeta-prime zero in each negative interval and no other zeros there.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A reflected auxiliary function moves right-half-plane derivative zeros to critical-line argument variation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines J through zeta, zeta-prime, and gamma factors so zeros of zeta-prime correspond to reflected J zeros, then proposes counting via arg J on one-half using differentiated Riemann-Siegel asymptotics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Normalize kth derivatives and read their horizontal zero displacement from a boundary integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Normalizes the Dirichlet series to one at right infinity, applies Littlewood's lemma on a wide rectangle, controls right and horizontal boundaries, and uses differentiated functional-equation asymptotics on the left to obtain both the total zero count and a weighted sum of real parts.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A critical-line mean bound converts the weighted identity into two-sided clustering

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Approximate-functional-equation and random-matrix routes independently predict the same high moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source frames the absence of proven higher moments, states the sixth- and eighth-moment targets, and treats agreement with the contemporaneous random-matrix calculation as independent support rather than derivation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two complementary Dirichlet polynomials are conjectured to carry the full zeta moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Stationary-phase analysis suggests the cross term is lower order, leading to a mean-square decomposition whose polynomial lengths multiply to the conductor scale and whose known validity boundary exposes the central extrapolation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Long Dirichlet-polynomial moments are controlled by shifted coefficient correlations, not diagonal orthogonality alone
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Montgomery-Vaughan theorem explains the short-polynomial regime; beyond length T, the problem becomes estimating coefficient sums and additive correlations, reducing high zeta moments to an unproved additive divisor problem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A delta-method main term plus square-root error predicts long divisor-polynomial moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Conjecture 3 specifies a smooth shifted-divisor main term and error, while Conjecture 4 turns that input into an explicit length-dependent moment weight w_k, creating a falsifiable bridge from additive correlations to zeta moments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Beyond length T squared, additive-divisor errors must create a new main term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The k=2 specialization contradicts Ingham if the conjectured error remains negligible past eta=1, so the paper diagnoses an accumulated error main term and restricts its high-moment construction to k at most four.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Diagonal size brackets the unknown moment constant and random matrices choose the intermediate scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Known lower-bound methods, the long-polynomial conjecture, and the expectation that diagonals dominate yield broad order-two growth bounds for g_k; the Keating-Snaith product gives a sharper asymptotic lying within them.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The growth law of moment constants determines which maximal-order bound should be sharp
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Optimizing the elementary moment lower bound using asymptotics for the arithmetic factor shows that exponential-in-k and random-matrix-scale g_k lead to different maximal-order regimes, reversing the usual preference for known lower bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Additive twists and residues manufacture the conjectural shifted-divisor main term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The delta method expresses the h-shift through Ramanujan sums; additive character expansions and principal-character poles then identify P_k(x,q), G_k, and the divisor-sum form of the derivative of the main term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Matching singular parts yields a residue identity and a usable bound for shifted-divisor coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source relates the shifted-divisor Dirichlet series residue to squares of additive-twist residues, then bounds the local factors on a shrinking contour to prove the estimate needed for absolute convergence and later rearrangements.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A three-variable Euler product isolates universal zeta poles from the arithmetic factor a_k
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Packaging f_k(dx,d) into F_k exposes a product whose leading prime terms factor into zeta functions; evaluating the analytic remainder at the origin recovers precisely the arithmetic Euler product appearing in moment conjectures.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The off diagonal becomes a fractional-part integral whose T-independent bulk cancels
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After symmetrizing the mean interval, expanding termwise, and inserting the shifted-divisor main term, the sine kernel sums to a fractional-part expression; its minus-one-half component is independent of T and disappears in J(2T)-J(T).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Laurent extraction turns the surviving off diagonal into the explicit weight w_k(eta)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The generating function is inserted into the fractional-part integral, leading Laurent terms are isolated, changes of variables reduce the result to residues gamma_k(n), and diagonal plus off-diagonal pieces assemble into Conjecture 4.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Complementary polynomial lengths erase eta from the sixth moment but force the eighth-moment constant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The identity w_3(eta)+w_3(1-eta)=42 makes every permissible approximate-functional-equation split agree, while k=4 admits only the symmetric endpoint and produces 24024, providing internal checks stronger than a single fitted length.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Splitting primes at k squared gives matching upper and lower asymptotics for the arithmetic factor
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Small primes supply the dominant Mertens factor, while elementary binomial bounds show the large-prime tail contributes only o(k squared) logarithmically, proving log a_k equals minus k squared times log of 2 e-gamma log k to leading order.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The introduction gives the reusable construction: integrate log zeta times a chosen kernel around an expanding rectangle, show the remote edges vanish, and evaluate the result through poles and zeros using generalized Littlewood theory.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Same-sign off-line zero corrections make a weighted argument identity equivalent to RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A positivity analysis bounds kernel parameters so every zero with real part greater than b contributes with the same sign; equality without the zero sum is therefore equivalent to a zero-free half-strip and becomes an RH criterion at b=1/2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Kernel parameters can expose explicit constants, including a removable collision with zeta's pole

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Changing to a double-pole rational kernel makes the residue at a+b proportional to zeta'/zeta and yields a new same-sign zero correction, producing a second family of zero-free half-strip criteria.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The repeated-kernel identity is equivalent to absence of zeros to the right of b

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Multiplying by z-1 cancels zeta's pole and links vertical and real-axis modulus integrals

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Volchkov and Balazard-Saias-Yor criteria are transformed versions of one log-zeta identity

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Eliminating nuisance constants opens a path from zeta factorization to analytic discriminant bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Stark's variant of the Hadamard-factorization identity removes two hard constants; differentiation and later Guinand-Weil kernels then improve bounds and clarify exactly what the method requires and cannot see.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positivity turns the explicit formula into a constrained kernel-optimization problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: To bound discriminants without special zero or prime data, one chooses even kernels whose arithmetic and spectral contributions are nonnegative; unconditional and GRH cases impose different positivity domains and therefore different optimization problems.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Optimal main terms do not settle the shape or remainder of the best kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Both unconditional and GRH settings have best-possible main terms, yet it remains open whether optimizers are scaled copies of one fixed function and how small the remainder can be.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local-completion constraints recast discriminant bounds as a global realization problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Serre's viewpoint generalizes prescribed real/complex completions to arbitrary local fields and, in the function-field case, turns minimal discriminant into minimal genus with a required number of rational points.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Root-discriminant invariance converts lower bounds into class-number bounds, but infinite towers defeat monotone-growth intuition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Hilbert class field preserves root discriminant while multiplying degree, so discriminant lower bounds constrain class number; Golod-Shafarevich towers then show why the once-expected divergence of minimal root discriminants cannot hold generally.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Field-discriminant methods do not automatically transfer to polynomial discriminants
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The survey isolates a nearby problem outside the analytic method's reach and explains the missing bridge: a field may lack a power basis, so a generator's polynomial discriminant need not equal the field discriminant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: High derivative positivity reconstructs a shifted Landau-Stark bound under GRH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Elkies differentiates the logarithmic-derivative identity, suppresses one term at high order, and uses carefully truncated Taylor expansions whose zero contributions remain positive, recovering a GRH-quality bound without Guinand-Weil.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Known small prime ideals permit kernels tuned to local arithmetic information
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Kernels optimized with no local data decay too quickly to exploit known ideals; alternative explicit-formula kernels emphasize specified norms, and exclusions such as no norm-2 prime ideal sharpen the resulting bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic ideal-class zeta methods trade Euler-product control for richer Minkowski conclusions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Geometry-of-numbers bounds control small ideals in every class, not just discriminants; Zimmert recovers improved ideal norms analytically, while the lack of an Euler product explains why GRH cannot simply be imported into the method.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta methods also produce regulator lower bounds with different small- and large-degree strengths
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Zimmert, Friedman, and Friedman-Skoruppa provide related analytic constructions for regulators, exposing a parallel optimization problem in signature and discriminant variables.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit-formula identity lets an inaccessible zero contribution be measured by subtraction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For small-discriminant fields, compute small prime-ideal norms directly, evaluate their explicit-formula contribution, and subtract from total deficiency to infer the aggregate low-zero contribution without computing zeros themselves.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the weighted Hilbert space criterion, its characteristic-function form, Baez-Duarte's restriction to integer scales, and the plan to reduce RH to basis-coordinate convergence plus a square-summable dominator.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Periodic antisymmetry turns HP into an odd-cosine Fourier space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proves completeness in HP by folding the weighted norm to the unit interval, multiplying by a sine factor, and identifying the transformed basis with the canonical odd-frequency cosine basis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dilates of the first basis vector are dense in the ambient Hilbert space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs periodic-antisymmetric approximants for compactly supported functions, bounds their norm, and rescales them to convergence; it also contrasts this quantitative construction with Wiener's Mellin-transform criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite coefficients cancel the first n basis errors exactly

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The triangular tail reduces RH to uniform control on a moving intermediate range

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Net-zero observations cannot by themselves certify Artin holomorphy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source isolates the obstacle to a finite verification algorithm: Brauer gives a ratio of entire functions, numerical zero locations remain uncertain, and a pole with a nearby canceling zero can evade naive comparison.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A common L-function contract supports all three certification layers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Euler product, completed functional equation, analytic conductor, allowed poles, and Ramanujan-type bound specify exactly what the explicit formula, Turing method, and FFT evaluator may assume.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Heilbronn characters convert pole cancellation into cone constraints
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Factoring monomial L-functions and Dedekind zeta functions constrains every possible zero or pole through nonnegative pairings; under the tested simple-distinct-zero hypothesis, indecomposability of an irreducible character forces observed net counts to be actual counts.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Almost monomiality is an indecomposability test in a dual character cone

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Failure of Artin certification need not block Dedekind-zeta RH certification
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: SL2(F5) exhibits induced-representation information insufficient to expose hidden poles, the adjoint-square route suggests a converse-theorem workaround, and a weaker multiplicity condition still certifies RH even when full holomorphy cannot be shown.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A constrained quadratic-form minimum becomes a zero-exclusion certificate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Weil's explicit formula evaluates bandlimited spectral probes from finitely many coefficients; positivity and normalization at a test ordinate turn the best probe into a computable infimum whose value below one rules out a zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Laurent coefficients of zeta's logarithmic derivative split each Li coefficient into two binomial sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 1 derives the central decomposition into an eta sum S2, an explicit zeta sum S1, and elementary terms, making separate cancellation mechanisms available for study.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Odd-integer expansions turn S1 into a monotone sum with an n log n lower bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Equivalent sum representations and a decreasing comparison integrand yield a rigorous lower bound for the positive contribution in the Li decomposition, while keeping the linear-term limitation explicit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The S1 estimates map directly into Dirichlet and Hecke Li formulas
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewriting the parity-dependent elementary terms in terms of S0, S1, and S3 shows exactly which part of the Riemann-case machinery transfers to extended RH settings.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Eta coefficients are recursively generated from Stieltjes constants
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The recursion exposes eta as the coefficient-level consequence of multiplying zeta by its logarithmic derivative, giving a direct computational and inductive bridge between two coefficient systems.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reciprocal-zero power sums equal an eta coefficient minus a simple zeta tail
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 3 links the local Laurent data at one to global nontrivial zeros and proves the bridge by reordering a successive zeta sum; it is the key identity behind the decay conjecture.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Evaluation of the eta generating series supplies exact moments and forces both signs
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Values and derivatives of the logarithmic-derivative expansion give signed sums, weighted moments, and beta-integral identities, ruling out one-sided eta behavior and constraining any proposed asymptotics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Removing the sigma term suggests alternating eta decay at the nearest trivial-zero scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 5 is rigorous, while Conjecture 1 combines the exact sigma-eta identity, the first nontrivial zero's faster decay, and the positive odd-zeta tail to predict eta sign alternation and magnitude decay.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A conjectural square-root bound on S2 would make Li positivity eventually automatic
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The span isolates the actual missing inference: eta alternation alone is insufficient, and a quantitative binomial-cancellation estimate must be combined with the rigorous S1 lower bound to obtain a Li lower bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The proposed proof route depends on magnitude correlation, not merely sign alternation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The summary explicitly identifies the remaining need to relate consecutive eta magnitudes, limits the numerical evidence, and explains which sum estimates plausibly transfer to generalized L-functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Comparison integrals, hypergeometric reductions, and contour residues provide complementary controls on binomial zeta sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Appendix A develops reusable ways to estimate S1-like alternating sums, including sharper integral bounds, generalized S0/S3 comparisons, digamma inequalities, and a contour-integral alternative for asymptotics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An integral zeta representation evaluates the successive sum underlying the sigma-eta bridge
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The appendix shows that the crucial reordered sum can be evaluated by interchanging summation and integration, providing an independent justification and two useful companion zeta sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Coefficient comparison in the logarithmic derivative of xi gives the sigma-eta identity directly
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expanding the digamma contribution and equating powers of s minus one bypasses the successive-sum computation, clarifying that the identity is intrinsic to the xi factorization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Tabulated Li and eta values exhibit positivity and near one-third alternating decay through index one hundred
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The table is the paper's direct computational evidence for its eta approximation and positive initial Li coefficients, while remaining nonproof evidence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dirichlet and elliptic-curve Li formulas isolate oscillatory arithmetic sums from explicit positive terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The appendix derives lower bounds in which the unresolved content is concentrated in character- or curve-weighted von Mangoldt sums and argues, conditionally, that sign/phase cancellation may make them small.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Product expansions and polygamma values reproduce the Dirichlet and elliptic Li formulas
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Differentiating completed L-functions shows systematically how gamma factors produce elementary zeta sums and logarithmic derivatives produce arithmetic von Mangoldt sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Dedekind construction reaches an explicit coefficient template but leaves convergence justification open
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Completed Dedekind zeta differentiation separates discriminant, gamma, and prime-ideal contributions, while explicitly stopping short of a final formula until the resulting series is justified.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Shifted and scaled binomial zeta sums reduce to hypergeometric comparison integrals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introducing shift nu and multiplier kappa unifies S0, S1, and S3, with terminating hypergeometric forms and digamma reductions furnishing a family of lower bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Factoring out six trivial zeros enlarges the eta expansion radius and changes the Li decomposition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The appendix makes representation dependence explicit: accounting for nearby trivial zeros moves the convergence barrier from three to thirteen, creates faster-decaying residual coefficients, and yields modified Li lower bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integral representations recursively express zeta and logarithmic-derivative moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Differentiating the Mellin integral organizes higher zeta derivatives and logarithmic-derivative moments needed by the eta moment problem, rather than treating each derivative as an isolated identity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A finite-difference polynomial is simultaneously hypergeometric, Laguerre, Mellin, and Laplace data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The same polynomial used in Li-related transforms is re-expressed as an associated Laguerre derivative, making the transform pair and its structural origin transparent.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-counting bounds control the tail of reciprocal-zero power sums under RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The appendix derives a local zero-density bound from Backlund's count and then, conditionally on RH, converts it into an explicit tail estimate for sigma power sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An imaginary-quadratic Dedekind xi integral forces real-axis positivity and derivative signs
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Positivity of the quadratic-form kernel yields positivity of xi on the real axis and nonnegative derivatives for s at least one-half, providing a structural result rather than a numerical observation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler-Maclaurin isolates alternating corrections to the main S1 comparison integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Arbitrary derivatives of the summand feed an asymptotic Bernoulli expansion, suggesting successive upper and lower approximations while explicitly warning that the series is generally divergent.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The extremal gap separates explicit Selberg bounds from genuinely optimal pair-correlation bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 1, Gallagher's half-integral construction, the two-delta obstruction, and the three-part roadmap distinguish an easy explicit family from the weighted extremizer and from the kernel quantity that limits any such bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Translated sign extremizers majorize and minorize an arbitrary interval
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Beurling's sign-function extremizers are symmetrically translated to produce admissible interval bounds for every beta, yielding an explicit series for their pair-correlation cost and a computable asymptotic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A weighted Paley-Wiener kernel solves the two-point interpolation obstruction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Equivalence of the pair-correlation and Paley-Wiener norms creates a functional Hilbert space; its explicit kernel converts minimum mass under two point constraints into a two-vector Gram problem with a closed-form extremizer.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The pair-correlation Hilbert space is identified isometrically with a de Branges space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source introduces Hermite-Biehler data and its kernel, reconstructs E from the pair-correlation kernel, and proves equality of the weighted norms, permitting interpolation and orthogonality tools unavailable in the original measure representation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Interlacing kernel nodes split the optimal interval problem into four regimes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The general weighted majorant/minorant problem is classified by whether the interval endpoint is a zero of A or B or lies between interlacing zeros, with auxiliary E_beta spaces supplying the generic interpolation nodes and exact quadrature sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A positive pair-count lower bound yields a small-gap result even without a simplicity dichotomy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source explains when an extremal minorant becomes nontrivial, states the improved 0.606894 threshold, and shows that either simplicity transfers the count bound to consecutive gaps or infinitely many multiple zeros force gap liminf zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 8 isolates the error condition under which fixed-band Selberg functions still control a growing pair window, separates the multiplicity correction, and derives unconditional-on-simplicity corollaries from a multiplicity bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Montgomery's nonnegative statistic evaluates admissible zero-difference sums on the known Fourier band
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Fourier transforms of the Selberg functions are computed explicitly, inserted into Montgomery's uniform formula, and compared with weighted interval counts while diagonal multiplicities are kept separate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier-series expansion gives an exact weighted cost for scaled Selberg functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof rescales the interval extremizers to arbitrary bandwidth, decomposes the weighted integral into elementary and cotangent terms, and evaluates the latter by a finite Fourier expansion and a limiting series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An analytic periodic series is shown constant, isolating the first correction to Selberg cost
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uniform convergence, Morera's theorem, differentiation under the series, and Riemann-Lebesgue cancellation show that the oscillatory component is constant; evaluating at zero produces the beta-asymptotic for arbitrary bandwidth.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier support and an integral equation determine the pair-correlation reproducing kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The construction uses norm equivalence and Fourier cancellation to verify a three-term explicit kernel; it also exposes the integral equation whose differential reduction determines the two free coefficients.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An uncertainty principle prevents bandlimited mass from hiding at the zero of the weight

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two pointwise constraints reduce to the geometry of two equal-norm kernel vectors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A general Hilbert-space lemma solves the minimum-norm problem under two modulus constraints; Krein factorization turns every nonnegative admissible function into a vector, so the lemma proves the two-delta formula and classifies equality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The one-point kernel norm recovers the optimal zero-multiplicity majorant

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mellin inversion converts analytic continuation and growth into coefficient-sum asymptotics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 2.12 and its corollary combine the Cahen-Mellin integral with an L1 Fourier-vanishing lemma and a Tauberian coefficient condition, giving a reusable bridge from vertical-line analytic control to smoothed and unsmoothed asymptotics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Regular boundary values and simple poles require distinct contour corrections
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The text modifies the general theorem first at c=0 by indenting around a regular boundary point, then at a simple pole by extracting its residue, thereby distinguishing convergence to F(0) from a main-term asymptotic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Power rescaling removes an artificial vertical-growth restriction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A condition suspected to be an artifact of the proof is removed by replacing the exponential kernel with a fractional-power kernel and translating the resulting coefficient estimates back to the original scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contour displacement turns a smoothed arithmetic series into a sum over zeta zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors move a Mellin contour left, classify residues from the pole, nontrivial zeros, and trivial-zero structure, then subtract a Bernoulli expansion to isolate a zero sum plus analytic remainder.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Under RH the smoothed error has exactly zero-forced scale, unlike the raw summatory error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A crude local zero count controls the explicit formula, giving an upper bound and both signs infinitely often; the authors then isolate the obstruction that the corresponding unsmoothed summatory function can be substantially less regular.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riesz means restore the regularity predicted by exponential smoothing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The section replaces Cesaro means by formally advantageous Riesz means, derives a zero expansion, and explains the Abelian implications in both directions between the smoothed theorem and the mean theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A completed L-function product bounds zero residues strongly enough to force signed bias
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof expresses a signed prime-power series by the logarithmic derivative of L(s), uses the functional equation and a canonical product to bound the zero contribution, then separates prime and higher-power terms to obtain a uniform negative main effect.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integral representations transfer divergence through power and logarithmic weights
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Two integral transforms show how a lower bound for a generating function survives insertion first of n^{-s} and then of 1/log n, completing the passage from a log-weighted prime sum to Tschebyschef's asserted unweighted bias.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: First-order Riesz means expose the same prime-race bias and imply exponential versions Abelianly
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors pass from exponential sums to Riesz/Cesaro means, isolate prime, square, and higher-power contributions, and prove a diverging negative first-order mean, clarifying which direction is merely Abelian.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Bessel-Mellin transform plus an integral Tauberian lemma yields the critical-line second moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The section converts a squared Mellin integral into a divisor-weighted Bessel series, obtains its boundary asymptotic, and uses a Tauberian integral lemma to recover the mean value of |zeta(1/2+it)|^2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Ramanujan reciprocal-series identity is isolated from the unproved contour estimate it needs
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors derive a striking symmetric candidate formula, then state precisely that a horizontal-contour bound or controlled bracketing is missing even under RH; this is a valuable example of separating formal residue calculus from a valid proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reciprocal cosine-transform pairs induce matched Mellin functional equations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Ramanujan's observation is abstracted from the Gaussian to reciprocal function pairs, whose Mellin transforms inherit a functional equation and parallel integral transformations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Decay of an entire Möbius-weighted function is equivalent to RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A reciprocal relation suggests a decay estimate, Mellin inversion shows why that estimate implies RH, and a known RH-conditional bound on Mertens sums proves the converse.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Partial summation reduces a family of weighted zero sums to one endpoint estimate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After stating the RH-conditional weighted exponential-sum bound, the authors show that the general weight exponent follows from a special case by partial summation, with uniformity in the phase parameter tracked explicitly.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contour residues are localized to the stationary range and bounded by a five-term error decomposition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof removes horizontal and local-zero contributions, expands the logarithmic derivative, splits integers by whether the phase has a stationary point, treats tails by first-derivative bounds, and controls the central range by quadratic approximation before summing five errors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A small signed integral conflicts with constant sign through a second contour evaluation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: To force a critical-line zero, the authors first reduce sign change to a short-interval integral estimate, then show that constant sign would turn that estimate into an impossible vertical zeta integral with a main term proportional to the interval length.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Dirichlet-series phase analysis supplies a zero of odd order in every sufficiently long short interval
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The remaining integral is expanded and split according to a phase's location relative to the interval; tail estimates and at most one central term complete the sign-change bound, yielding many odd-order zeros on the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Simultaneous approximation aligns finitely many zero phases to force logarithmic oscillation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors rewrite the prime-counting error as a convergent sine series over zero ordinates, approximate it by a model exponential sum, control the tail, and apply Dirichlet simultaneous approximation to transfer one large value to arbitrarily high phases.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A modified Lindelof principle moves interior growth to a discontinuous boundary limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Because the model function is not continuous on the boundary, the authors formulate and prove a strip lemma with local boundary control, global boundary bounds, and interior growth, then apply it contrapositively to transfer the oscillation estimate to the boundary series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Passing from psi oscillation to pi-Li needs smoothing beyond partial summation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source explains why ordinary partial summation loses the one-sided Omega information, introduces a prime-power corrected counting function, and uses the earlier Riesz-mean bound to show the correction is negligible at the target scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A two-parameter approach to critical-line zeros is abandoned after a stronger unrelated method appears
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The introduction records how an attempted parameter coupling suggested a short-interval zero theorem but remained incomplete, while a different proof removed dependence on both Mellin and elliptic-function machinery; it also records the still-unsuccessful stronger density target.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A persistent finite-range prime-counting bias is overturned by a slower-growing oscillatory term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors explain why extensive computations can support a false global inequality: a fixed-sign lower-order term dominates until an iterated logarithm grows enough for the oscillation to emerge, and the same method predicts reversals in residue-class prime races.

section_argument_map.label: 4 Zeros on the critical line

section_argument_map.label: 5 Oscillation of psi(x)-x and pi(x)-Li(x)

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Real nonvanishing as a family-level alternative to universal exceptional zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates forced or arithmetic central vanishing from the quadratic Dirichlet expectation and motivates proving a positive family proportion rather than individual GRH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positive proportion of quadratic L-functions with no real zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the main 20 percent positivity conclusion and the related thin zero-free rectangle and zero-density consequence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Selberg kernel converts a real zero into a positive boundary integral inequality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The cut-contour argument produces a positive weighted sum over zeros; functional-equation pairing then gives a uniform lower bound whenever a nontrivial real zero exists.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Geometric-mean control reduces exceptional discriminants to mollified second moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces the squarefree family average, weighted exceptional count, normalized mollified moment W, and the arithmetic-mean/geometric-mean step that replaces averages of log absolute values by log W.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exceptional-count bound and moment targets J1 and J2
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Packages the zero-count problem into two explicit integrals of a normalized mollified moment and begins the gap-producing choice of coefficients.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Coefficient gap offsets exponential growth of Selberg's kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Chooses a piecewise polynomial mollifier so the product L times M has vanishing low Dirichlet coefficients, forcing the boundary moment rapidly toward one where the kernel is largest.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Completed product and squarefree-tail decomposition for the central moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reparameterizes two shifts, derives a smooth approximate functional equation for their completed product, and splits squarefree detection into a tractable main part and a long-divisor remainder.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson-evaluated main term with individually and averagely controlled remainder
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the four-residue main term, two complementary remainder bounds, regularity of the singular-looking sum, and the specialization that yields the usable normalized moment.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit parameter choice closes the positive-proportion theorem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Substitutes the moment asymptotic into the weighted zero bound, reduces it to two finite integrals of V, and records a computer calculation giving 0.79 below the critical threshold one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why Selberg's kernel forces a gap mollifier and limits box height
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains the core representation change from boundary argument to log magnitude, the resulting exponential-kernel cost, the mollifier-length versus box-size tradeoff, and the unresolved coefficient optimization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symplectic low-zero repulsion explains the small weighted zero count
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the proved threshold argument from a GRH and Katz-Sarnak heuristic predicting a much smaller contribution, then identifies repelling families as plausible transfer targets.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetric approximate functional equation for a product of completed values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The weight's residue asymptotics and exponential decay justify a contour reflection whose two residues combine, by the functional equation, into the desired product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gauss-sum local structure, quadratic large sieve, and Poisson dualization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Links prime-power Gauss evaluations and real-character moment bounds to a Poisson formula that turns a squarefree character average into zero and nonzero dual frequencies.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contour truncation and character averaging make L times M close to one off center
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the engineered coefficient gap, contour shifts, square cancellation, large-sieve estimates, and a zero-free Dirichlet-series region to prove both the normalized moment estimate and control of the far boundary.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Normalized zero clusters turn local spacing into n-level correlations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source moves from unit-mean normalized ordinates and level repulsion to translation-invariant test functions that count clusters, making the GUE determinant a precise observable rather than a spacing metaphor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Restricted-support GUE universality depends on primitivity and a universal second moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorems 1.1-1.2 and the remarks separate the proved support range from the full conjecture, show why products of primitive factors lose level repulsion, and identify Rankin-Selberg second-moment universality rather than coefficient-law universality as the causal input.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contour shifting converts a smoothed zero sum into prime powers and archimedean terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proposition 2.1 and its proof show how the Euler product, functional equation, and a rapidly decaying entire test function combine to express zero statistics through logarithmic-derivative coefficients while keeping the pole of zeta explicit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Rankin-Selberg pole forces the universal quadratic coefficient mass
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The local identity for L(s,pi times pi-tilde), its simple pole at one, and a Tauberian argument yield a universal log-squared asymptotic for the weighted coefficient mean square, explaining the analytic source of GUE universality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Higher prime powers are isolated as the only technical gap and controlled through degree three
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Hypothesis H cleanly separates higher-prime-power convergence from the Rankin-Selberg main term, and Proposition 2.4 proves it for degrees at most three by ordering Satake parameters and feeding the resulting bound back into Rankin-Selberg convergence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unrestricted smoothed correlations expose pairings before distinctness is restored
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source deliberately replaces distinct-index correlations by unrestricted sums, Fourier-represents the test function, and states a pairing measure whose disjoint index pairs will later be sieved into the true n-level statistic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Applying the explicit formula coordinatewise factorizes the correlation into signed prime sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Each Fourier coordinate is split into archimedean, positive-prime, and negative-prime components, so expanding the product reduces the zero statistic to structured sums C_{r,s} with transparent sign choices and coefficient products.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier support makes approximate multiplicative balance exact and suppresses the off diagonal
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compact support bounds the product of prime-power variables; localization plus integrality then turns near equality of two integer products into exact equality, while divisor-type L2 estimates show the discarded off-diagonal range is lower order.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Only balanced prime pairings survive at main-term scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After rescaling the diagonal integral, Rankin-Selberg bounds show configurations with unequal positive and negative counts or repeated higher prime powers are lower order; distinct primes must match by a permutation, producing the disjoint-pair formula in Theorem 3.1.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The natural support boundary changes with poles and coefficient cancellation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors explain that zeta's polar term and Dirichlet-character prime correlations cause saturation at total support two, whereas cusp-form coefficient cancellation should preserve diagonal dominance farther than the proved degree-dependent range.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Approximation and RH transfer the smoothed theorem to sharp height cutoffs and local spacing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Positive majorants extend the admissible cutoff class to characteristic functions, and a mean-value comparison shows that height-dependent local normalization and fixed log-T normalization differ only below the main scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Möbius inversion on set partitions removes repeated zero indices
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Coincidence patterns among indices form the partition lattice; unrestricted and distinct correlation sums are related by its zeta transform, so Möbius inversion reconstructs the desired n-level statistic from lower-dimensional unrestricted sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Collapsed correlation pairings and GUE cycles reduce to one subset identity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Fourier pullback under each partition embedding yields delta distributions for collapsed blocks; after Möbius inversion, comparison with the cycle expansion of the GUE determinant reduces the theorem to the identity X_S=(-1)^{|S|-1}Y_S.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Permutation cycles factor the Fourier transform of the sine-kernel determinant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expanding the determinant by permutations, decomposing into disjoint cycles, and applying Parseval turns each cycle into an interval-overlap integral, explaining structurally why determinant combinatorics can match prime pairings.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A convex-envelope bijection evaluates the cycle overlap by maximal walk deviation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Partial sums are interpreted as a closed real walk; interval intersection gives one minus its range, and Spitzer's unique rotation plus upper-convex-envelope blocks counts maximal deviations by set partitions, proving the final subset identity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Langlands quotients reduce non-tempered local factors to tempered building blocks
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The appendix represents a generic unitary local component as a Langlands quotient, factors its L-function through tempered pieces, and reduces those further to square-integrable data, making local analytic bounds a statement about real Langlands parameters.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Twist classes expose ramified Rankin-Selberg factors as positive quadratic products
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Supercuspidal twist classes and segment representations turn the ramified Rankin-Selberg factor into products of conjugate quadratic terms; logarithmic expansion then gives nonnegative Dirichlet coefficients and bounds the local parameters.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Global holomorphy bounds archimedean Langlands parameters
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The classification of real square-integrable factors and their Rankin-Selberg products locates the first possible archimedean pole; global holomorphy to the right of one then forces every real parameter inside the half strip.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Nonnegative Rankin-Selberg coefficients turn Landau's theorem into uniform local bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Landau's coefficient estimate, applied to the globally continued nonnegative Rankin-Selberg series, bounds powers of unramified parameters and, through the ramified coefficient inequality, yields the same improvement at every finite place.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Function spaces, dilation spans, and Mellin coordinates for the closure problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Establishes the shared language in which the criterion is posed: vanishing and compactly supported function classes, the fractional-part kernel, bounded dilations K_lambda, the generated space B(g), and the Mellin transform analytic on the critical strip under the stated Lp hypothesis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Muntz operator measures a sum-integral discrepancy and commutes with dilation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines P f as the difference between an extended sum of dilates and a scaled integral, then identifies dilation commutation as the structural property used to move generated spans through P and related operators.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The strong Nyman-Beurling criterion becomes a Muntz-generated closure problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the classical L2 closure equivalence, identifies direct Gramian computation as a stalled Hilbert-geometry route, uses P chi=-rho_1 to re-express the theorem, and formulates the search for kernels satisfying the analogous closure equivalence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Strong kernels form a dilation-stable cone whose additive closure is unknown
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explores the generalized kernel family: step functions with zero-free Mellin transform provide examples, scalar multiplication and dilation preserve strength, addition is not known to do so, and this failure motivates restricting attention to a differentiable subspace with potentially tractable scalar products.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weighted derivative control forces decay and all-Lp integrability of good kernels
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the good-kernel class and proves from integration by parts that t f(t) tends to zero, ruling out a nonzero limiting constant by L1 integrability; this supplies the decay and integrability prerequisites used throughout the Muntz analysis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Good kernels yield universal necessity but only compact-support sufficiency with a Mellin zero condition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the paper's central asymmetry: RH sends every good kernel into the closure of dilates of P f, while compactly supported good kernels satisfying that closure can only force zeta zeros in the right half of the strip to be zeros of f-hat; a zero-free f-hat upgrades this to an equivalence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Burnol's weighted sum bound makes the Muntz series well defined almost everywhere
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses two monotone-convergence rearrangements and a counting-function bound to control the sum of |f(nx)| with dx/x, yielding almost-everywhere existence and local integrability of P f for good kernels.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Multiplicative convolution imports Young's inequality and factors every good kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the invariant operator T_F, proves its Lp norm bound by rewriting it as ordinary convolution on the multiplicative group with Haar measure dt/t, and records f=-T_{f'} chi, the identity later used to transfer Nyman-Beurling approximants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: P f is pseudo-convolution of f-prime with rho_1, with an Lp bound and a sharp endpoint warning
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gives an alternative definition P f=T_{f'}rho_1, derives Lp control for p>1, explains why P is not continuous in the ordinary Lp norm because the derivative remains exposed, and identifies rho_1 not in L1 as the endpoint obstruction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integration by parts and Burnol convergence identify the sum-integral operator with pseudo-convolution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands T_{f'}rho_1 through P chi, controls the integral term using t f(t) to zero, converts the indicator sum into truncated samples f(nx), invokes Burnol's lemma for absolute convergence, and recovers the defining sum-integral expression for P f.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Muntz's formula turns P into multiplication by zeta under the Mellin transform
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the transform identity (P f)-hat=zeta times f-hat, shows that the nonsmooth characteristic kernel already realizes the proto-Muntz formula, and links this identity to the functional equation and Nyman-Beurling criteria before extending it to all good kernels.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pseudo-convolution factorization proves Muntz's formula with an explicit Fubini certificate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Substitutes P f=T_{f'}rho_1 into the Mellin integral, separates variables using the proto-Muntz identity, integrates by parts to obtain f-hat, and repeats the calculation with absolute values to justify the interchange for every point in the critical strip.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The necessity route tests RH without requiring a nonvanishing kernel Mellin transform
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The author frames the generalized necessity condition as a possible disproof test using analytically tractable kernels and stresses that, unlike the earlier proof for chi, it requires no Mellin-transform condition on the chosen kernel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A bounded dilation-invariant operator transports classical approximants to every good kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Starts from RH-conditioned approximants to -chi in B(rho_1), applies T_{f'} to them, uses commutation with dilations and P f=T_{f'}rho_1 to land in B(P f), and uses f=-T_{f'}chi plus L2 boundedness to preserve convergence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Compact support blocks analytic kernels, while the expected Lp extension lacks matching necessity theory
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies removal of compact support as the immediate open improvement needed to admit analytically promising kernels, and records the expected Lp half-plane analogue together with the precise reason it is not claimed: neither necessity direction has been worked out in that setting.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mean cancellation and compact support convert L2 closure into pointwise Mellin vanishing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: At a zeta zero in the right half of the strip, applies V=I-2K_2 to the approximating family, creating a compactly supported mean-zero F whose P F and generated approximants vanish beyond a common bound; Muntz's formula kills their Mellin values, and Cauchy-Schwarz on the bounded interval passes the zero to F-hat and hence f-hat.

section_argument_map.label: 2.1. Existence of P f

section_argument_map.label: 2.2. A convolution operator

section_argument_map.label: 2.3. P as a convolution operator
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Represents the Muntz operator as pseudo-convolution against the fractional-part kernel, records mapping properties and endpoint failures, and proves the representation.

section_argument_map.label: 2.4. Muntz's formula
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Relates Mellin transformation of P f to multiplication by zeta, connects the general formula to the proto-Muntz identity, and proves it with an absolute-convergence check.

section_argument_map.label: 3.1. The necessity criterion

section_argument_map.label: 3.2. The sufficiency criterion
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Records the compact-support and prospective Lp boundaries, then uses a mean-cancelling dilation operator and bounded-support Mellin evaluation to force zeros of the kernel transform.

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The original pair chi and -rho_1 is sent by the bounded dilation-intertwining operator T_{f'} to the pair -f and P f, so RH-conditioned closure approximants transfer functorially to every good kernel instead of requiring a new Gramian calculation for each one.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: This proves only the RH-to-closure necessity direction, depends on the established strong Nyman-Beurling theorem and good-kernel regularity, and does not make the resulting scalar products computable.

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The same operator is certified as an almost-everywhere sum-integral discrepancy, represented as dilation convolution against rho_1, and diagonalized by the Mellin transform as multiplication by zeta; the existence, norm, and Fubini arguments connect these views rather than treating them as formal identities.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The bridge is proved only under the source's good-kernel/integrability hypotheses, fails at the stated L1 endpoint, exposes derivatives in physical-space continuity, and its exact formulas require PDF verification.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: P has complementary physical-space and Mellin-space representations

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Closure of f by dilates of P f, after mean cancellation and compactification, forces every zeta zero in the right half of the critical strip to be a zero of f-hat; choosing a compactly supported good kernel with zero-free Mellin transform would therefore turn this inclusion into an RH equivalence.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The source does not remove compact support, construct a new tractable zero-free analytic kernel, or prove the expected Lp analogue; the criterion relocates these obligations rather than solving them.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Sufficiency relocates the problem to zeros of the kernel Mellin transform

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The stalled route asks for explicit Gramian distances among fractional-part dilates, whereas the generalized necessity proof uses a bounded operator commuting with every dilation to preserve approximation abstractly and opens a search over kernels whose scalar products might be simpler.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The broader kernel family is only cone-like, additive closure remains unknown, and no kernel with demonstrably decisive scalar-product geometry is produced in this note.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Robin's criterion can be restricted to integers containing a fifth power
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Starts from the exact RH equivalence and narrows potential counterexamples through squarefree, odd, squarefull, and 5-free results until only integers divisible by a nontrivial fifth power remain.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A largest-prime dichotomy proves the squarefree class by either descent or Mertens control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Inducts on the number of prime factors: a largest prime above log n permits removal while preserving the inequality, whereas a smaller largest prime lets a prime-reciprocal bound dominate the logarithmic target.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The totient ratio transfers an odd problem to a squarefree kernel and then to the squarefree theorem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Upper-bounds sigma(n)/n by n/phi(n), observes the latter depends only on the squarefree kernel, and maps an odd squarefree product to a smaller even squarefree number whose Robin bound controls the original.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Primorial oscillation blocks extension of the stronger totient inequality to even integers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that n/phi(n) can exceed or fall below the Robin-scale target along primorials depending on RH, so the convenient stronger surrogate used for odd integers cannot prove the full even case.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-product bounds force any squarefull exception into a small finite search
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses an explicit Mertens product and a Chebyshev lower bound to cap the number of distinct prime factors, then uses squarefullness to bound the integer itself and reduces the theorem to an enumerated finite check.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler-product truncation determines maximal divisor ratios on t-free classes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates prime divisors above log n, bounds their aggregate effect, applies Mertens and the zeta Euler product below log n, and constructs matching extremal sequences from fixed prime exponents.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: If RH fails, dangerous exponent multiplicities must grow without bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines Robin's infinitely-many-counterexamples conclusion with bounded limsups on every fixed t-free class to show that counterexamples cannot remain within any fixed exponent cap.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sorting larger exponents onto smaller primes maximizes the divisor ratio for a fixed pattern
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proves a swap monotonicity lemma, defines the canonical Hardy-Ramanujan realization of an exponent pattern, and shows it is both the smallest integer and the largest sigma(n)/n among all realizations, so verifying it certifies the entire pattern class.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A minimal t-free counterexample must have largest prime below its logarithm
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Removes the largest prime, invokes minimality on the cofactor, and shows that a prime at least log n would make the multiplicative increase in sigma too small relative to the increase in log log n.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler-product tail bounds cascade the largest-prime threshold down to 73
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Bounds the t-free divisor ratio by a truncated Euler product plus an explicit tail, turns failure of Robin's inequality into a bound on log n, and repeatedly feeds the improved bound back to lower the possible largest prime.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Minimality forces the final 5-free counterexample to be Hardy-Ramanujan
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Maps the exponent pattern to its canonical minimum; minimality rules out a distinct canonical representative above 5040, while a representative below the cutoff yields a final bounded-support estimate and finite contradiction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The same method does not cheaply advance from 5-free to 6-free
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records that strengthening the exponent cutoff would require substantial computation and points to a structurally different proposed approach.
