result_and_mechanism_map.title: The predicted bias gives a one-sided lower bound while RH leaves an alpha-dependent error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the paper's unconditional discrepancy lower bound and its RH-conditioned interval-count inequality, showing exactly which half of the conjectured behavior is currently forced and what residual size remains.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniform cancellation of zero exponential sums would upgrade smooth tests to intervals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies sums of x to the i-gamma as the Fourier quantities controlling interval counts, formulates their required uniform cancellation range, proves that range sufficient under RH, and compares it with what Landau's formula and zero-density estimates already provide.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The explicit formula translates zero cancellation into prime regularity in short intervals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States a short-interval prime conjecture sufficient for the zero-sum conjecture and a converse implication with a weaker error, then contrasts both with a Gaussian fluctuation heuristic and known RH bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A weighted two-zero energy can certify one-frequency cancellation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces the pair-correlation function as a quadratic representation of zero spacings, formulates the strengthened uniform asymptotic actually needed below the classical Montgomery range, and shows it implies the same zero-sum and discrepancy conjectures.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positive smoothing converts the smooth-test asymptotic into an interval discrepancy witness
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Convolves a maximizing interval indicator with a nonnegative approximate identity, applies the known smooth asymptotic, uses boundedness of g_alpha under a small translate, and extracts at least one shifted interval realizing the lower bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Extremal trigonometric polynomials sandwich an interval with controlled Fourier cost
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces the discontinuous interval indicator by majorant and minorant polynomials of degree J whose constant-term error is optimal, then couples their frequencies to uniform Landau estimates up to a source-chosen cutoff J0.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Resonant Fourier modes reproduce g_alpha while nonresonant modes average away
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands the polynomial counts into zero exponential sums, applies Landau's formula frequency by frequency, identifies prime-power modes exactly when alpha is resonant, and proves uniform convergence makes every other mode o(T); this derives the source's bias rather than assuming it.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Choosing the truncation scale separates the unconditional RH error from conjectural tail cancellation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Collects the bias integral, optimal constant-coefficient error, and unresolved high-frequency zero sums, then uses J=J0 for the RH bound and J proportional to log T followed by a limit for the conjectural sharp result.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Beurling-Selberg entire function localizes an interval while compactly supporting its Fourier transform
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs an entire approximation F to the unit interval indicator from an odd sign approximant, obtains Fourier support in [-K,K], and records spatial decay plus uniform transform and derivative bounds needed to move between zero ordinates and prime scales.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Band limitation turns a zero sum into local differences of the prime-counting error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Splits the sharp zero sum into a band-limited part and controlled approximation error, integrates by parts, substitutes the explicit formula, cancels the constant contribution, and bounds the result by variation of G(y)=psi(y)-y in a multiplicative neighborhood of x.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-sum cancellation fed backward through the explicit formula controls prime increments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Writes a prime increment as a truncated sum over zero contributions, controls medium and high ordinates using the exponential-sum conjecture plus partial summation, treats low zeros trivially, and obtains the converse error in Theorem 3.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A tunable pair-correlation kernel bounds the linear zero sum through local second differences
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Normalizes pair correlation, introduces a beta-scaled kernel G_beta, invokes a quadratic-energy bound for the zero sum, and rewrites G_beta as an exponentially weighted average of F(xe^u,t), pairing u and -u so that only a second difference of D remains.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Small normalized pair-correlation variation at beta just above log T forces the target cancellation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies the strengthened pair-correlation conjecture uniformly to the three nearby x-scales in the energy lemma and chooses beta slightly larger than log T so both resulting terms are o(T).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Selberg-class axioms preserve the analytic/Euler duality and introduce degree as the zero-density scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the analytic continuation, functional equation, Euler-product logarithmic derivative, coefficient growth, degree, zero count, primitive factorization, and generalized critical-line hypothesis that make the zeta mechanism portable to a larger L-function class.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A zero-density substitute plus a generalized Landau formula supplies the extension's local input
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States Hypothesis Z_F measuring decay away from the critical line, records classes where it is known, and gives the uniform explicit formula whose main term selects the nearest integer carrying Lambda_F; these replace the zeta-specific inputs in the earlier argument.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The resonant fractional-part bias persists for primitive Selberg-class L-functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines g_{F,alpha} from prime-power logarithmic coefficients and proves the same two-term distribution for C2 tests under zero density and for absolutely continuous tests under RH_F, with an unconditional Dirichlet-L corollary.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Dirichlet character phase predicts where fractional zero ordinates should be scarce
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Specializes the bias to L(s,chi), reads its phase as a shortage near specified residue locations, and compares the predicted curve with histograms from a finite zero table while clearly presenting the plots as illustration rather than proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: General L-function interval conjectures inherit the same one-sided theorem with a theta_F loss
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Formulates indicator and discrepancy analogues and derives the generalized lower bound and RH_F interval error, making visible how coefficient growth enlarges the Fourier cutoff cost.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Generalized zero sums and short-interval coefficient errors remain dual through G_F
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Adjusts the zero-sum lower range for theta_F, gives the generalized explicit formula for weighted coefficients, and states both directions between cancellation and short-interval variation of G_F under RH_F.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: For degree at least two the pair-correlation transition falls outside the useful explicit-formula window
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the degree-scaled pair-correlation conjecture, identifies its change of behavior near x=T^{d_F}, and explains why the degree-one proof transfers but degree at least two requires control through a transition region not reached by the available Landau estimate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A bounded, smoothly varying pair-correlation profile repairs the transition-zone failure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Formulates uniform boundedness and a local second-difference condition for D_F, precisely matching the symmetric variation term in the earlier energy lemma, and records that this stronger condition restores the generalized zero-sum and discrepancy conclusions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Purity emerges from placing one variety in a family and testing all tensor powers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains Deligne's methodological shift: use monodromy representations of a parameterized family, locate poles by invariant theory, and combine arbitrarily high tensor powers with positivity to force every local eigenvalue onto the target circle.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A power saving makes the cusp error smaller than the local-density main term

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Robin's pointwise inequality and Gronwall's limsup frame a record-value search for RH counterexamples
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source distinguishes a universal post-5040 bound from an asymptotic maximal-order statement, reviews other thin-sequence criteria, and explains why record holders of sigma(n)/n are natural counterexample candidates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Infinitely many extremely abundant record values are equivalent to RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: XA is defined by successive records of sigma(n)/(n log log n) after 10080; the least Robin counterexample must be such a record, while RH plus Gronwall prevents the record sequence from terminating.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Near-multiplicative bounds can be inverted without losing logarithmic control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The auxiliary lemmas transport relative x-y bounds through log and log-log factors and establish monotonicity inequalities later used to compare consecutive abundant numbers.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit Chebyshev bounds and oscillations connect largest prime factors to log n
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Upper and lower estimates for theta, psi, pi, prime gaps, and the Mertens product provide both finite effective inequalities and sign-changing asymptotics used to separate SA, CA, and XA behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Record maximality forces ordered prime exponents and psi(p) below log n
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Comparing a superabundant number with multiplicatively modified competitors constrains every prime exponent by the largest prime, yields p asymptotic to log n, and identifies psi(p) as a lower structural bound for log n.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit theta and psi estimates give two-sided control of p around log n for SA numbers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Bounding the contribution of repeated small-prime powers compares log n with theta(p), then explicit prime-function estimates invert the relationship to place p inside a narrow relative window around log n.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Superabundant divisor ratios approach Gronwall's constant from an explicit two-sided envelope
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A lower comparison with n/phi(n), an explicit Mertens product, and the p-versus-log n bounds yield f(n) tending to e^gamma along SA, complementing Robin's global upper estimate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Record dominance can persist under nonlinear divisor-sum transformations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source proves monotonicity of sigma(n)-n and stronger log-log adjusted or exponentiated expressions along SA by combining consecutive-record inequalities with bounded ratios and the asymptotic lower bound for sigma(n).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A single epsilon parameter converts CA maximality into prime-by-prime exponent thresholds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The CA variational definition yields threshold functions x_k and a finite Euler-product construction, including the exceptional ambiguity when a threshold is prime; Robin's adjacent-CA maximum theorem then makes CA a scaffold for f-records.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An XA record between consecutive CA numbers forces the upper CA endpoint to be XA
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Robin's adjacent-CA maximum principle transfers any intervening record to the next CA number, proving infinitely many CA-XA intersections under RH; Chebyshev oscillation also constructs infinitely many CA numbers with largest prime exceeding log N.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Removing the largest prime from an XA record forces p below log n
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A direct comparison of f(n) with f(n/p), followed by elementary logarithmic inequalities, proves the strict largest-prime bound characteristic of XA.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Opposite largest-prime inequalities force infinitely many CA numbers outside XA
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 4.31 supplies infinitely many CA values with p greater than log N, while every XA has p below log n, so the two abundant classes cannot eventually coincide.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A gap condition makes sigma(n)/n plus phi(n)/n increase across XA records
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof balances the gain in the XA divisor-ratio record against the totient loss from a new largest prime, using explicit prime-product estimates and a lower bound on the multiplicative gap.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite XA data suggest rigid exponent transitions, monotone prime support, and gap laws
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The numerical section records bounded exponent changes between consecutive XA values, monotone largest prime and divisor count, counterexamples to stronger implications, and multiple empirically monotone compositions that can seed later conjectures.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Treat the Riemann zeros as a secondary zeta spectrum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces Dirichlet series over transformed nontrivial zeros, their Hurwitz-like shifts, and the goal of compiling explicit meromorphic data rather than treating isolated special cases.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Spectral-zeta methods transfer only after singularity accounting
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares the Riemann explicit formula with Selberg trace formulas, then explains why the Riemann secondary zetas need a separate treatment: their poles are double and the most symmetric parameter makes the naive explicit formula diverge.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Stage the analysis by base point and half-plane
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lays out an abstract Delta/Zeta framework, first explicit base point, general shifts, a symmetric special case, and later Hurwitz refinements, with separate treatments of polar and special-value half-planes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Choose an admissible product that minimizes order and pole complexity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines a sequence through convergence, a normalized Weierstrass product, and a differentiable generalized Stirling expansion, then explains why reducing both growth order and logarithmic degree simplifies the resulting zeta continuation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Asymptotics at infinity and Taylor data at zero continue in opposite directions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a Mellin transform of log Delta: the generalized Stirling expansion generates poles on one side, while the Taylor expansion generates positive-integer data on the other; sine and gamma factors then cancel or lower pole orders.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pair functional-equation zeros and square the spectral coordinate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Groups zeros under the functional symmetry, rewrites the entire completion as an even Hadamard product in s(1-s), and thereby replaces an order-one zero sequence with a simpler order-one-half squared sequence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The large-parameter expansion fixes the secondary-zeta poles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Substitutes the inverse quadratic branch into the completed-zeta Stirling expansion and translates its coefficients into a sequence of half-integer poles, a regularized determinant, and negative-integer trace values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Taylor coefficients give two descriptions of positive zero sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands the same Delta product through zeta at s and 1-s, equates coefficients, and obtains finite identities connecting secondary-zeta values with derivatives at zero and cumulants of Stieltjes constants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Shifts make polar data polynomial but finite-point values transcendental
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares a simple normalized Hadamard product with a fully translation-covariant regularized determinant and shows that large-parameter coefficients transform polynomially in the shift, while Taylor coefficients at a finite point depend on zeta and its derivatives.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Move to the symmetric shift to gain a better continuation formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Chooses the shift centered at s=1/2 because the transformed factorization is most symmetric and its secondary zeta, though numerically close to the earlier one, has a substantially simpler continuation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Treat trivial zeros and the pole as a signed shadow spectrum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Interprets the gamma-factor zeros as a trivial-zero spectrum and the zeta pole as a negative-multiplicity ghost eigenvalue whose combined determinant cancels the nontrivial-zero growth.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Split the Mellin transform into shadow and nontrivial resolvent pieces
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces resolvent traces for trivial zeros and the ghost pole, rotates around their singularities, evaluates the shadow contributions by residues, and leaves a regular integral with broader continuation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A shadow term carries all polar and trace data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains that the non-elementary integral is regular in the relevant half-plane, so the explicit shadow term alone determines poles and integer trace identities; cancellations at positive arguments also expose which transcendental zeta values remain unknown.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The spectral analogy breaks at pole order but suggests an L-series template
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies precise mismatches with compact-surface spectral zetas, notes the coexistence of additive and multiplicative copies of zeta, and abstracts the factorization/Mellin method to Dirichlet zeta or L-series with their own trivial spectra.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Expand every shift around the symmetric solvable case
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a binomial expansion around the symmetric shift to import meromorphic continuation, pole parts, and terminating negative-integer trace identities to arbitrary shifts.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Combine a more singular zero sum into a less singular Hurwitz function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands another Hurwitz-like sum around the symmetric secondary zeta, then shows that a particular combination cancels all but one pole and converts its derivative at zero from a regularized zero product to a Hadamard product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Repeated integration by parts turns logarithmic asymptotics into pole order
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gives the reusable continuation argument: each asymptotic power yields a Mellin pole, and a polynomial of degree p in log z raises that pole to order p+1; reversing zero and infinity handles the other half-plane.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Replace unstable zero partial sums by analytic continuation formulas
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a density-based tail integral to accelerate zero sums, observes that erratic spectral fluctuations defeat raw and Cesaro regularization below a threshold, and switches to the continuation integrals for stable evaluation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Modified PT symmetry constrains eigenvalue pairing but not reality

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Sketches a finite-interval cutoff and logarithmic renormalization under which a transformed position expectation scales like Lambda divided by log Lambda.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that dilation splits a log-correlated field into a divergent scalar Gaussian mode and a universal spatial chaos, and formalizes the stable object projectively modulo nonzero constants.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Organizes the proof around truncated Euler products, explicit two-point limits, Hilbert-transform estimates, negative-Sobolev tightness, randomized prime phases, and a Gaussian-plus-smooth logarithmic decomposition.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States subcritical and critical chaos limits for the randomized model, then isolates precise zeta moment and correlation asymptotics as the obstacle to transferring them to actual shifts.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A discrete Fourier-sampling norm embeds weighted test functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces the V and Z norms and proves that logarithmically sampled Fourier values are controlled by a weighted L2 norm through a point-mass-to-interval estimate in W^{-1,2}.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The zeta boundary kernel equals the discrete norm in the oscillatory limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Computes a distributional Fourier transform and uses it to identify the Z inner product with a shifted zeta kernel whose pole produces the singular-integral term while the oscillatory remainder vanishes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Shifted two-point asymptotics control Euler-product approximation for every test function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns Ingham-Bettin-type two-point asymptotics into uniform second-moment bounds and proves that zeta and its truncated Euler product become close for fixed weighted test functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lift scalar test estimates to Sobolev convergence and close the two-limit diagram
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Integrates Fourier-mode estimates to get W^{-alpha,2} approximation, constructs the randomized Euler product as an L2-bounded Hilbert-space martingale, and closes the T then N approximation by Wasserstein triangles.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite Dirichlet polynomials bypass mixed Euler-product estimates
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Provides a second proof route using finite Dirichlet polynomials and cross moments, clarifying which quantitative approximation strength is lost when explicit truncated-product two-point estimates are avoided.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic continuation exists off the line, but the boundary is not locally a measure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses Poisson extension and local uniform Euler-product convergence to obtain a zero-free random analytic function for sigma>1/2, then proves boundary blow-up almost everywhere and excludes measure-valued boundary restrictions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniform convergence and exponential regularity for random function series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Packages Sobolev embedding, Levy maximal inequalities, Borel-Cantelli, and concentration into a reusable criterion for smooth random-series limits with exponential norm moments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Separate smooth higher prime powers and Gaussianize frozen prime blocks
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows higher Euler-product powers are smooth, groups first-order prime terms into slowly varying blocks, freezes phases within blocks, and couples each block to an isotropic Gaussian with quantitative error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Choose block growth so coupling and freezing errors converge smoothly
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives separate summability criteria, selects an explicit superpolynomial block sequence, controls incomplete blocks, and obtains a full Gaussian-plus-smooth decomposition with exponential C^ell bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Complex chaos is an L2 Sobolev martingale and the residual error is a smooth multiplier
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs the Gaussian exponential as a Hilbert-space martingale and passes the logarithmic Gaussian approximation through test functions to identify zeta_rand=e^E nu.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Construct high-frequency complex chaos through analytic boundary values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Represents Gaussian fields by Brownian Fourier integrals and obtains a uniform second moment for exponential high frequencies by analytic continuation, the Plemelj formula, and L2 boundedness of the Hilbert transform.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Replace Gaussian prime sums by a Brownian logarithmic-frequency integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the prime number theorem and Ito isometry through three controlled approximations to transform the prime-indexed Gaussian field into an integral with u^{-1/2} spectral weight plus a smooth error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mesoscopic dilation factors into smooth correction, divergent zero mode, and scale-invariant chaos
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Decomposes the dilated Brownian integral at frequencies delta, 1, and delta times the cutoff, proves the chaos law is independent of delta, and transfers the result back to zeta by a diagonal choice of scales.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime covariance is logarithmic up to a smooth remainder
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the Gaussian-chaos convergence criterion and proves that the real Gaussian prime field has covariance one-half log(1/|x-y|) plus a smooth term, uniformly controlled near the diagonal.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Comparable normalizers and smooth errors transfer subcritical chaos to the randomized zeta model
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows the true exponential normalizer is uniformly comparable to the Gaussian one, then uses Lp martingale bounds and the smooth coupling error to prove nontrivial subcritical convergence and supercritical degeneration.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Construct the critical measure by bounded covariance comparison
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Chooses a reference white-noise approximation with known critical convergence, reshapes the spectral weight to match its covariance, verifies bounded/off-diagonal covariance differences, and transfers convergence back through smooth independent factors.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives shifted divisor-sum asymptotics from effective Perron inversion, contour movement, zeta growth, and the functional equation, including the classical second moment as the zero-shift limit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Translate contour moments into uniform two-point kernels

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Bounds W1 by local Fourier-density discrepancy and tails, smooths a normalized sum by a small Gaussian, treats nearly degenerate covariance directions separately, and upgrades mean coupling error to exponential moments.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Absolute convergence licenses exchanging the sum and contour integral; moving the path collects the zeta and pole terms, then the functional equation and gamma-pole residues produce finite corrections plus a remainder, with a free smoothing parameter containing a known formula as a special case.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After reflecting zeta and recentering the contour, the proof bounds the integral with an even increasing gamma ratio, rescales it by a decreasing function, evaluates the tail as an incomplete gamma function, and obtains a numerical remainder bound whose coefficient growth diagnoses the useful truncation range.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Real exponential smoothing forces a length-t cutoff and a finite optimal correction series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Setting the incomplete-gamma parameter to one makes the main sum exponentially smoothed, but asymptotic decrease of the correction terms requires K greater than t/(2pi), hence a Gram-type cutoff; the free power p accelerates decay while lowering optimal truncation and attainable accuracy.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A concrete critical-line specialization supplies a computable Z(t) expansion and analytic remainder bound; tables compare optimal and deliberately suboptimal truncations, showing high accuracy for modest M but rapid deterioration of the bound well before the formal least term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Increasing cutoff scale buys accuracy, while increasing smoothing power can destroy it
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The final numerical comparison separates two effects: larger K extends the effective main sum and improves attainable accuracy, whereas larger p sharpens exponential decay but shortens the asymptotic correction series enough to reduce total accuracy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The functional equation reduces moment analysis to four vertical regimes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines I_sigma(T,k), explains why integer k exposes a Dirichlet-product structure, and separates the easy half-plane, boundary, critical strip, and critical line as genuinely different analytic cases.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Absolute convergence makes the diagonal main term and uniformly bounded off-diagonal explicit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands zeta^k into divisor coefficients, separates m=n from m not equal n, integrates the phase, and uses absolute convergence for sigma>1 to prove a linear main term with O(1) error and hence all short intervals with H tending to infinity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: At sigma=1 a renormalized error replaces absolute convergence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the mean-square error after subtracting its linear and logarithmic terms, records pointwise and mean bounds, and explains how a Hooley-Huxley contour obtains asymptotics for complex powers and logarithmic derivatives.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Second and fourth moments in the strip require distinct refined error structures
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts the two-term mean-square formula with fourth-moment asymptotics and a spectral refinement whose lower-order terms can be smaller than the available error outside a restricted sigma range.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta moment thresholds and divisor-problem variance control opposite ends of the strip
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the general remainder, the threshold sigma_k-star from bounded moments, and beta_k from integrated divisor errors, then shows their two estimates are complementary near the threshold and near one and ties the uniform family to Lindelöf.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An optimal double-exponential kernel transports a nonvanishing half-plane value into a short-interval lower bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a rectangle residue formula with Ramachandra's kernel, suppresses horizontal sides double-exponentially, averages the transported estimate, and optimizes the auxiliary scale to prove the moment cannot be too small.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two different oscillatory formulas encode the critical-line mean-square error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines E(T), presents Atkinson's two-sum formula and a Riemann-Siegel double-sum alternative, explains how either controls local zeta values, and relates current upper bounds and omega results to the shortest available mean-square interval.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gaussian smoothing turns the fourth moment into a Laplacian spectral sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the fourth-moment error, introduces Motohashi's smoothed fourth moment, and explains how the Bruggeman-Kuznetsov trace formula exchanges Kloosterman sums for Maass spectral data, yielding upper/omega bounds and a short-interval scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Higher critical-line moments remain blocked by additive divisor correlations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts random-matrix conjectures with the absence of proved asymptotics even under RH, states the Lindelöf-equivalent family of moment bounds, and identifies a ternary additive-divisor conjecture sufficient for the sixth moment.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The short-interval lower bound fixes the logarithmic scale that an upper bound should match
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the Balasubramanian-Ramachandra lower bound, contrasts trivial RH control with Soundararajan's sharp full-interval upper bound, and identifies large values of log|zeta| as the correct upper-bound interface.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH yields nearly sharp polynomial-length short-interval moments but not the log-log regime
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the author's RH-conditional H=T^theta upper bound, matches its logarithmic exponent to the lower bound up to a vanishing correction, and explicitly records the inaccessible shorter range and known unconditional exceptions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A three-regime large-deviation law for log|zeta| integrates to the moment bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States Gaussian-like and V log V tail estimates across three V ranges, dyadically partitions log|zeta|, and optimizes 2kU-U^2G to recover the k-squared logarithmic moment exponent.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Under RH, large log|zeta| forces one of two prime sums to be large
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines a smoothed von Mangoldt majorant, removal of prime powers, and a high-moment lemma for prime Dirichlet polynomials, then chooses x,z,A in three V regimes and splits the event between short- and long-prime sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: High even moments and scale-dependent r choices prove the three tail regimes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies the prime-polynomial moment lemma separately to both forced sums, chooses r to satisfy the short-interval length constraint, and combines the resulting Gaussian and V log V decays to establish every range of the large-value theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands tau_A and tau_B as ell-fold convolutions, records that pair ordering becomes meaningful, and prepares each paired factor for a separate rational approximation.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces discrete convolution sums by additive-character averages, rescales variables so the product cutoff is Perron-detectable, and packages all factors into LHS_ell for comparison with the recipe.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 1 states the central bridge between the delta-method expression and the recipe's arithmetic factor after choosing one shift from every paired block.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Summing all sign patterns factorizes the multidimensional Fourier integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rotates positive and negative integration paths and iterates the gamma integral, changing an entangled sign-summed kernel into a product of chi factors used by the zeta functional equation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Residue extraction cancels Perron remainders and exposes the recipe's Euler product
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands shifted-divisor averages near their poles, sums h_j to zeta factors, cancels crossed poles against removed truncation residues, and uses chi times zeta to reduce the global theorem to one prime-local identity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A complicated rational-direction Euler factor collapses to a swapped diagonal correlation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces coefficient-generating functions and states Theorem 2, the local identity that turns all compatible rational directions into a diagonal C(A,B) factor with swapped shifts.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poles of a multiple Dirichlet series encode mean values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper's central representation change is explicit: treat a family average as one coefficient direction of a several-variable Dirichlet series, so continuation in the averaging variable and a pole at one become a route to moment asymptotics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite functional-equation groups mark the last uniquely controlled cases
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It links three phenomena: a finite reflection group, uniqueness of local correction factors, and continuation by convex hull; when the group becomes infinite at degree four and above, uniqueness and reachable continuation fail together. The cubic moment theorem is positioned as the last fully controlled quadratic-family case.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A local continuation neighborhood would suffice despite a distant singularity barrier
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors distinguish global perfection from the smaller continuation actually needed for moments: the central moment point lies beyond the group-generated region but before the expected essential-singularity curve, so a local continuation hypothesis could still determine all main-term coefficients.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic and geometric moment factors meet at a polar residue
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It separates the Euler-product arithmetic factor from the random-matrix geometric factor and proposes a multiple Dirichlet series whose w=1 residue produces both; slight continuation beyond that divisor would turn the prediction into a theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Oscillation continues the integral series and isolates the diagonal pole
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expanding zeta factors turns the integral into oscillatory kernels. Integration by parts continues nonstationary kernels to Re(w)>0, while the unique nonoscillatory multiplicative constraint contributes the simple pole at w=1; divisor bounds prove the remaining sum converges.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The diagonal residue factors into universal zeta poles and a local arithmetic constant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The multiplicative equality constraint yields an Euler product; extracting pairwise zeta factors leaves a holomorphic remainder whose central specialization is precisely the conjectural arithmetic factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Stirling asymptotics turn individual zeta reflections into an affine group action
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The exact zeta functional equation and an asymptotic gamma expansion produce quasi-functional equations for the integral series. Tracking the oscillatory index identifies the subgroup that preserves the pole-bearing sector and hence the reflections of its basic polar hyperplane.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reflected polar hyperplanes plus Tauberian positivity imply the zeta moment law
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The conjecture freezes the needed continuation and polar divisor near the central point. Subtracting the full orbit of a model pole leaves a holomorphic remainder, and a Wiener-Ikehara theorem converts the leading Laurent coefficient into the even-moment asymptotic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetry cancels all nonconstant Taylor data in the leading polar coefficient
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After centering variables, the orbit sum is put over a common product of polar hyperplanes. Alternation and divisibility remove apparent singularities, and homogeneity shows positive-degree Taylor terms vanish in the normalized limit, leaving a combinatorial constant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic-family symmetry predicts all moments but the direct continuation breaks at the fourth
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Known first through cubic moments and the symmetry-type constants are synthesized into a general conjecture; the authors identify insufficient functional equations near the first significant pole as the concrete failure mode for m at least four.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Splitting signs and residue classes makes the quadratic-family series reflection-invariant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The raw discriminant sum is decomposed by sign and congruence and multiplied by gamma factors; the individual quadratic-L functional equations then become a finite Abelian action on the completed several-variable series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic reciprocity reduces the w=1 pole to square products
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After expanding the L-functions and moving the discriminant sum inside, quadratic reciprocity rewrites it as square-free character Dirichlet series. Their continuation shows a pole occurs only when the combined index is a square, giving an exact residue selection rule.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Extracting universal zeta factors identifies the quadratic-family arithmetic constant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The square-product residue has an Euler product. Removing the one-variable and pairwise zeta singularities leaves a holomorphic factor whose central value matches the conjectured family arithmetic factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: All 2^m reflected poles generate the quadratic-family moment polynomial
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The finite reflection group sends the base w=1 pole to hyperplanes all meeting at the central point. The continuation conjecture asserts these are the complete local divisor, and a Tauberian reduction makes their joint principal part sufficient for the moment asymptotic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Antisymmetry and divisibility make the quadratic orbit sum finite and universal
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A common-denominator argument shows the symmetrized orbit sum has removable singularities; homogeneity kills all higher Taylor terms, so a convenient one-parameter specialization computes the universal geometric factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Correction polynomials preserve the primitive functional equation off the square-free locus
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The cube is viewed as a GL(3) Eisenstein L-series. For imprimitive quadratic twists, local Dirichlet polynomials are required to satisfy dual functional equations, square-class compatibility, and an interchange-of-summation identity; these conditions are uniquely determining through GL(3) and cease to be so from GL(4).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A finite character vector closes under both s- and w-reflections
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Changing the order of summation and applying the dual correction-polynomial identities yields one reflection in w; the GL(3) functional equation yields another in s. Packaging finitely many bad-prime characters into vectors turns both into meromorphic matrix equations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A dihedral reflection group and tube convexity propagate continuation to C-squared
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Initial convergence estimates give a tube region after canceling base poles. Alternating the two affine involutions produces overlapping reflected tubes whose convex hulls successively expand to all of C-squared; explicit orbit factors cancel the transported polar hyperplanes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Several-variable holomorphy controls a one-variable vertical specialization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Functional equations bound the completed series on outer tubes; a domain-of-holomorphy argument fills a bounded hole in the real base, proving the central one-variable specialization has finite order and enabling Phragmen-Lindelof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional-equation paths give strip bounds and rule out artificial bad-prime poles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Fourth-moment input bounds the absolutely convergent edge; repeated reflections control the opposite edge. Analytic deformation in two variables excludes poles introduced by finite Euler-factor denominators, leaving only the base pole and its genuine reflected candidate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Möbius inversion reconstructs the fundamental-discriminant series from perfect building blocks
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A divisor parameter enforces square divisibility, a second Möbius sum removes every nontrivial square factor, and character combinations restore sign, congruence classes, and the Euler factor at 2. Bounds remain summable beyond Re(w)=4/5, while the Section 3 residue calculation gives the seventh-order pole.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A smoothing kernel converts the seventh-order pole into a degree-six moment polynomial
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Mellin inversion with the weight 1-|d|/x permits shifting to Re(w)=4/5+epsilon; the pole at one supplies the full logarithmic polynomial and the vertical bound controls the new contour.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Short-interval second moments control truncated Perron error for signed cubic coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Because cubic central values are not assumed nonnegative, unsmoothing needs local coefficient control. A short-interval second-moment estimate plus a global fourth moment and Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the near-cutoff part of truncated Perron, while absolute convergence handles the tails.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The unweighted sum is reduced to vertical, horizontal, and reflected-pole contributions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shifting the truncated Perron rectangle separates the seventh-order main pole, a possible 3/4 pole, the new vertical integral, horizontal integrals, and truncation errors; the sieve parameter is then split into large and small ranges with different contour choices.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Second-derivative cancellation saves a half power in the reflected vertical integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reflecting the vertical integral into absolute convergence produces a ratio of gamma products. Stirling expansion exposes a phase with controlled second derivative, and a van der Corput-type lemma yields cancellation beyond an absolute-value estimate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Separate large and small sieve moduli, then equalize the dominant errors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A divisor reparameterization controls sums over the sieve modulus. Large moduli use a near-one contour; small moduli use the oscillatory estimate. Collecting four dominant powers and solving their balance yields the published error exponent subject to the short-interval constraint.

section_argument_map.label: 2.1 Multiple Dirichlet series for zeta
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Constructs oscillatory integral series, continues them past absolute convergence, isolates the pole at w=1, and factors its residue into zeta factors and a holomorphic arithmetic factor.

section_argument_map.label: 2.2 Quasi-functional equations
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses the zeta functional equation plus Stirling expansion to define a finite affine action and identify the subgroup preserving the zero oscillatory index.

section_argument_map.label: 2.3 Fundamental zeta conjecture
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Conjectures continuation and reflected polar hyperplanes, applies a Tauberian theorem, and computes the leading moment coefficient by cancellation in a group-orbit sum.

section_argument_map.label: Quadratic-L moment background
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Defines the quadratic family, records known low moments, and states the symmetry-type prediction for all integral moments.

section_argument_map.label: 3.1 Quadratic-family multiple Dirichlet series
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Completes signed discriminant series, derives their functional equations, identifies the square-index contribution to the w=1 residue by reciprocity, and recovers the arithmetic factor.

section_argument_map.label: 3.2 Fundamental quadratic-family conjecture
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: States the reflected-pole continuation conjecture and derives the predicted moment constant by a Tauberian reduction and a symmetric group-orbit limit.

section_argument_map.label: 4 and 4.1 Cubic foundations
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Represents the cube as a GL(3) Eisenstein L-series and specifies correction polynomials whose functional equations and interchange identity complete imprimitive twists.

section_argument_map.label: 4.2 Coupled cubic functional equations
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Builds a double Dirichlet series and packages its w- and s-reflections as finite-dimensional matrix functional equations, including the exceptional local behavior at 2.

section_argument_map.label: 4.3 Several-variable analytic continuation
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses tube domains, convex hull extension, and a dihedral group of affine involutions to continue the cubic building block meromorphically across C-squared after explicit pole cancellation.

section_argument_map.label: 4.4 Vertical-strip control
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Proves finite order, propagates bounds by functional equations and convexity, and excludes spurious poles while retaining the reflected candidates at w=3/4 and w=1.

section_argument_map.label: 4.5 Sieve to fundamental discriminants
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses Möbius inversion and character combinations to remove square factors, transfer analytic control to the primitive family, compute the seventh-order pole, and obtain the weighted asymptotic.

section_argument_map.label: 4.6 Unweighted estimate
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Combines short-interval mean bounds, truncated Perron integrals, functional-equation oscillation, a large/small sieve-parameter split, and exponent optimization to remove the smoothing.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Microscopic normalization seeks a function, not merely a zero process
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why sine-kernel convergence of zeros does not by itself produce a canonical analytic object and why dividing nearby characteristic-polynomial values can remove the divergent common amplitude while retaining zero geometry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Normalize the CUE characteristic polynomial at mean spacing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the rescaled entire ratio xi_n, states compact-open convergence in law to an entire function with sine-kernel real zeros, and explains why the ratio has stable size although either characteristic-polynomial value does not.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Virtual isometries convert weak limits into an almost-sure analytic coupling
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs Haar matrices of every dimension from rank-one extensions, couples their eigenangles pointwise, and obtains an almost-sure compact-uniform limit expressed as a symmetrically paired product over the sine process.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Strong function convergence transfers ratios, logarithms, counts, and derivatives
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how one compact-open almost-sure limit yields microscopic ratio convergence, a fully correlated Gaussian leading mode for nearby logarithms, eigenvalue-count convergence through argument variation, and convergence of logarithmic derivatives.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Argument variation turns characteristic-polynomial concentration into eigenangle control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates the number of zeros on an arc to deterministic angular drift minus the change in the logarithm's imaginary part, proves a sub-Gaussian tail at one point, and uses rotation, a grid, Borel-Cantelli, and piecewise-linear interpolation for a uniform O(log n) bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Determinantal count tails yield logarithmic rigidity uniformly in n and k
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives mean, logarithmic variance, Bernstein tails, and exponential moments for interval counts, converts them to y_k=k+O(log(2+|k|)) for the sine process, and patches local coupling with a coarse finite-n bound to make the estimate uniform.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Periodic eigenangles become a paired canonical product
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the sine product and eigenangle periodicity to rewrite each finite ratio as a symmetric product over all rescaled zeros, then proves uniform tail control from logarithmic rigidity and closes pointwise-to-compact convergence with Montel's theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero rigidity bounds the entire-function order
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Splits paired product factors into three index regimes to obtain an exponential O(|z| log |z|) upper bound and compares the imaginary-axis product with the sine product for an exponential lower bound, proving order one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One-point intensity extends microscopic linear-statistic convergence to every L1 test
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Truncates an arbitrary integrable test to a bounded compactly supported test, invokes known convergence there, and controls both tails uniformly using the common unit one-point intensity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero statistics are encoded by the imaginary logarithm
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Formulates a zeta-zero analogue with the extra logarithmic density weight and proves, by integration by parts against the counting function, that centered linear statistics of CUE zeros equal an integral of Im log xi_n against the test derivative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hadamard products match local zeta zeros to the sine-process resolvent
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Conjectures process-level convergence of a locally normalized zeta function and its logarithmic derivative, then derives a finite-height zero-resolvent expansion whose i pi term comes from the Archimedean gamma factor and matches the CUE limit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Index-symmetric and spatially symmetric resolvent truncations agree
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that cutting the conditionally convergent logarithmic-derivative sum by index or by |y_k|<A changes only O(log A) boundary terms of size O(1/A), hence gives the same value.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Block interval counts control exponential resolvent tails
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Partitions distant zeros into polynomially growing intervals, separates signed count cancellation from absolute count error, applies determinantal exponential moments through Jensen's inequality, and obtains a tail estimate uniform over finite n, the limit, and compact off-real z.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exponential tails give Lp resolvents and justify correlation-function moment limits
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns the exponential estimate into quantitative Lp decay for truncated resolvent tails, proves the full logarithmic derivative lies in every Lp off the real axis, and authorizes computing its moments from bounded-window sine-kernel correlations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sine-kernel correlations determine first and second resolvent moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Computes the first moment from unit intensity and the second moments from the diagonal term and the two-point sine kernel, then translates the result into a zeta logarithmic-derivative conjecture linked to pair correlation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Balanced ratios have moments and their expectations survive the function limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Bounds ratios by integrating the logarithmic derivative along zero-free off-real segments, combines near/far resolvent controls for all moments, and upgrades almost-sure compact convergence to locally uniform convergence of expected products of balanced ratios.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Giambelli compatibility produces an explicit limiting ratio formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the formal determinant identity for polynomial ensembles, carefully extends it to actual CUE analytic ratios by domain continuation and removal of an arc, computes the one-ratio expectation from rotational invariance, and passes the determinant formula to xi_infinity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The limiting determinant suggests a process-level zeta ratio law
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transfers the explicit xi_infinity ratio expectation to a concise microscopic zeta-ratio conjecture and records that RH plus GUE conjectures were shown elsewhere to imply it.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Audit reasons to doubt RH by explaining why their surprises are not surprising
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the paper's evidential burden, separates persuasion from proof, and makes multiple representations and levels of randomness the organizing method.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A zeta snapshot fixes local shape but hides the carrier scale
result_and_mechanism_map.unit_type: snapshot principle for absurdly large heights
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Argues that normalized local gap patterns recur with positive frequency and determine graph shape only up to a vertical factor, so visually similar windows can differ enormously in magnitude.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional equation, xi, and Hardy Z encode the same symmetry in different forms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates meromorphic zeta, entire xi, and real Hardy Z representations, then distinguishes the sign-symmetric Z distribution from the small mean bias of zeta.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH symmetry plus zero counting turns sign changes into a certified finite-height result
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States equivalent RH formulations, warns that interlacing pictures alone are insufficient, and explains the Turing-method comparison between critical sign changes and the total zero count via S(t).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unfolded zeros, S(t), and log|Z| separate typical from extreme scales
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Normalizes shrinking zero gaps and juxtaposes conjectural extreme bounds with Selberg's independent Gaussian bulk laws for log|Z| and S.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A computed large gap couples Z and S locally but cannot represent their typical independence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the largest computed examples and the exact gap-to-S increment to show why conspicuous finite-height events are atypical of the independent bulk distributions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Order-one computational bias masks the slowly emerging asymptotic scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Traces Gram-point bias to the first Riemann-Siegel term and explains why sqrt(log log T) remains indistinguishable from fixed-size effects throughout computationally accessible heights.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Four finite-height regularities become misleading global heuristics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates useful computational targeting from unsupported claims that large gaps, reinforcing initial terms, or Gram points reveal extreme values or likely RH failures.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Nearby zeros determine shape while distant zeros supply a slowly varying scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Factors a high-degree polynomial into near and far zeros and transfers the mechanism to Z, defining the three-part local description underlying carrier waves.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Carrier persistence plus growing variance lets one L-function dominate a linear combination
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains Bombieri-Hejhal's dominance mechanism and establishes that carrier variation drives the bulk value distribution while local gaps remain lower order.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Move equally spaced reference zeros to observed zeros to isolate the local carrier factor
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs a partial-Hadamard-product fit that divides out local zero spacing, interprets the remaining scale, and records its unavoidable window dependence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The functional equation supplies the loudest highest tone and the Dirichlet series perturbs it
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reframes the Riemann-Siegel formula as an almost band-limited spectrum, explains low-height Gram behavior, and generalizes the conductor-controlled highest frequency to L-functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Self-reciprocity turns the critical line into the unit-circle fixed locus
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows equivalent coefficient, functional-equation, reality, and reciprocal-zero conditions and identifies RH as the claim that every zero is fixed by the involution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Randomizing zeros, not coefficients, leads from unitary polynomials to the CUE
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rejects coefficient-random ensembles for the wrong zero law, defines circular beta repulsion, and selects beta=2 by qualitative rigidity and gap/value behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Brownian paths, tridiagonal products, and Haar unitaries realize the same beta=2 point law
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the eigenvalue distribution from its matrix realization and identifies quadratic repulsion, rather than matrices themselves, as the relevant local mechanism.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Repulsion controls limiting local statistics across Gaussian and circular ensembles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Places GUE, compact-group, and recipe eras in sequence, then uses determinantal kernels and their sine-kernel limits to explain local universality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The GUE hypothesis predicts local zero statistics but not zeta values or arithmetic corrections
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transfers pair correlation, simplicity, and extreme normalized-gap exponents while identifying missing primes, finite-height corrections, and value distributions as decisive shortcomings.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Keating-Snaith matches matrix degree to zero density and models values by characteristic polynomials
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains the N=log(T/2pi) calibration, finite-height non-Gaussian fit, moment constants, and the many-independent-polynomials model for an interval.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic dampens matrix extremes, while disc geometry models off-line zeta behavior
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why lower-order zeta corrections are less extreme, distinguishes Z from zeta modeling, and maps the right critical half-plane to the disk with derivative-zero compatibility.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Statistical rarity rescues predictions even when deterministic unitary analogues fail
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Classifies exact leading agreement, arithmetic-factor agreement, and deterministic failure, then shows why exponentially rare counterexamples need not occur in the prescribed random sample.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One degree-1000 characteristic polynomial contains regions differing by a factor of 500
result_and_mechanism_map.unit_type: carrier wave inside one unitary polynomial
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows within a fixed polynomial that comparable local gap variation can coexist with radically different scales and defines a zero-matching procedure for the local carrier.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weighted long-neighbor discrepancies reconstruct the carrier wave from complementary zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces individual gaps by local density, defines neighbor discrepancy, and gives a weighted sum whose empirical agreement with the independently fitted carrier is the core explanatory mechanism.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Product expansion derives the density weight and links carrier slope to S(t)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Factors out the cosine reference from paired zeros to justify inverse-neighbor weighting, then translates high or low density into average trends of S and carrier size.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Carrier waves require large interacting systems, fixing a hidden degree choice in the matrix model
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why density fluctuation is emergent and why rescaling a much larger single matrix creates excessive carrier amplitude compared with concatenating calibrated smaller systems.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Slow S(t) growth constrains long neighbor gaps and suppresses finite-height carrier waves
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses neighbor-spacing variance, its number-variance form, low-zero resurgence, and universal/non-universal regimes to connect arithmetic rigidity with limited density variation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Small gaps are universal while large gaps are sensitive to arithmetic rigidity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the small-gap exponent from quadratic repulsion, transfers its moment consequence, and warns that CUE tail estimates may overpredict zeta's largest gaps.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One large gap has proportional influence and only linear logarithmic effect
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates carrier and local contributions, constructs the most likely neighboring-zero configuration, scales its influence range, and uses a zero-moving product to bound its contribution to log|Z|.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Neither isolated large nor tiny gaps can supply the positive mass required by Selberg's CLT
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that gap-tail frequencies conflict with a large-gap explanation and that tiny-gap neighborhoods cannot occupy enough measure to explain typical small values, forcing a many-gap conspiracy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: For Lindelof questions the correct polynomial class is self-reciprocal, not necessarily unitary
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses Backlund's zero-density equivalence and a polynomial implication to distinguish largeness caused by radial off-circle zeros from largeness caused by angular irregularity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Derivative combinations share a carrier factor and therefore admit common mollifiers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why slowly varying amplitude survives normalized differentiation and motivates reciprocals of linear combinations of zeta derivatives as effective mollifiers.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime and zero descriptions are complementary coordinates joined by an adjustable product
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rejects causal overinterpretation, gives prime-based CLT intuition, separates universal short-range zeros from arithmetic long-range behavior, and presents a hybrid factorization whose parameter trades prime against zero information.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime phases and matrix traces produce clustered maxima and the FHK correction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the log-correlated-field heuristic in both worlds, explains clustered extremes, compares independent-sample maxima with the FHK law, and blocks an invalid tail extrapolation to global extremes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Short-interval maxima suggest a log-log carrier width, while fixed moments cannot identify the bulk wave
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Infers the number of correlated zeros from effective sample size, then explains why shifted positive or negative moments are dominated by atypical values and cannot measure the typical wave.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Moments of moments and Gaussian multiplicative chaos expose hierarchical structure beyond snapshots
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects freezing transitions to a randomized critical-line function and its factorization into a common GMC distribution times a smooth nonvanishing model-specific factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arbitrarily close pairs occur in unitary models where the RH analogue is exact
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the unitary-polynomial control to show that close critical zeros and several forms of 'barely true' stability do not shift evidence against RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Robust real-zero arguments are structurally mismatched to an RH that is barely true
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts stable special-function real-root mechanisms with the perturbation sensitivity attributed to xi and argues that purely analytic zero-spacing techniques cannot contain the deep part of a proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Large oscillations become ordinary after choosing snapshot scales
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Refutes a visual objection to extreme Z values by showing that spike density is axis-dependent and that many critical-line zeros force such appearances regardless of global RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A derivative identity needs both a large boundary term and a uniform high-derivative bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reconstructs Blanc's proposed contradiction, isolates the L-function-specific derivative theorem, and explains repeated differentiation as gap regularization toward a cosine attractor with a restricted derivative range.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Slow cosine attraction in unitary polynomials reframes Blanc's mechanism as a gap-bound problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows why unitary counterexamples need many derivatives, tests the coefficients in the proposed contradiction, and formulates a concrete polynomial problem whose solution might transfer to improved zeta gap bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two known moment errors do not justify an extrapolation that would negate Lindelof
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the historical moment method from unsupported pattern fitting, notes failures of optimistic error conjectures too, and distinguishes the genuine k=4 structural transition from error-term claims.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Linear combinations fail RH because they lose the Euler product, not because their functional equation is weak
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses carrier dominance to explain why almost all zeros may remain critical while transitions create off-line zeros, then sharpens the distinction by zeros in the absolute-convergence region and the missing Euler product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A false mechanism can still be an effective filter without becoming evidence about extremes or RH failure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why large-gap and short Riemann-Siegel filters can locate finite-height peaks, then reverses the off-line-zero heuristic and demands an explicit model of how RH would fail.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Precise Gram law tracks zero identity and is destroyed by large-scale sloshing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Restores Gram's original interlacing claim, translates its failure into S(t), and reconciles local random-matrix spacing with long runs displaced from expected Gram intervals.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Matched Haar-unitary data explain apparent Gram-point specialness as transient
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives reversal and sign symmetries in the matrix model, matches degree to height, and uses increasing degree plus lower-order corrections to explain good/bad and shifted-interval discrepancies.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A zero-first model makes density the scale-setting object and RH failures nonaccidental
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts a function-first view in which critical zeros look conspiratorial with a zero-first view in which explicit-formula constraints and density waves make each zero structurally meaningful.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Scalar projection as a spin-sensitive modular bootstrap
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why integrating out spin is normally lossy and why a scalar-only equation is a stronger, physically meaningful target; it also states the zeta-zero bridge and its Virasoro limitation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Roelcke-Selberg decomposition and the scalar-free cusp-form channel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Provides the representation change that makes scalar projection decisive: constants, a continuous Eisenstein family, and discrete Maass forms, with the latter integrating to zero in the scalar sector.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reduced partition functions and constrained Epstein zeta data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how subtracting an Eisenstein series restores square integrability and packages scalar dimensions into constrained Epstein zeta series with analytic continuation and a functional equation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Scalar crossing equation with residues at nontrivial zeta zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The vanishing scalar part of Maass forms collapses the decomposition; shifting the Eisenstein contour then turns nontrivial zeta zeros into explicit spectral correction powers.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From the contour remainder to a Möbius-hypergeometric spectral kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the functional equation and a Dirichlet expansion of a zeta ratio to exchange sums and integrals, evaluate the remainder as a confluent hypergeometric kernel, and check both numerically and asymptotically.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson-Mellin functionals that remove zeta-zero powers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Diagnoses sign-indefinite moduli and zeta-residue terms, removes the constant by differentiation, and constructs a rapidly decaying Poisson-resummed functional whose action on t^s contains ζ(s), hence vanishes at every nontrivial zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gaussian constraints and derivative sum rules
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Converts the abstract annihilator into constrained Gaussian combinations and then into derivative identities at k=1, exposing the vacuum contribution and the independence of even derivative orders.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Discretize, solve, and globally recheck positivity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records a reusable numerical-proof pattern: derive low-order asymptotics, discretize a non-polynomial positivity problem, solve it with SDPB, inspect the full continuum for negative regions, and iteratively resample.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bootstrap bounds versus the average Narain scalar gap
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates an optimal universal bound from an ensemble average and shows that their different large-c behavior is evidence about weakness of the chosen equation, not a contradiction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fake scalars for general Virasoro CFTs
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: When square integrability fails exponentially, multiplication by a cusp form creates a tractable but signed representation involving all spins; the source derives its crossing equation and explicitly flags a convergence gap in the derivation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why the Virasoro functional program loses positivity and convergence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies two separate blockers: the functional weakens exponential decay enough to lose against Cardy growth at c≥7, and signed character coefficients destroy eventual positivity across spin.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A numerically observed scalar-only Virasoro sum rule below c=7
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Presents an unexpected scalar-only identity, its null-state adjustment, convergence condition, empirical status, weak resulting bounds, and the proposed analytic-continuation route.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH as the envelope of subsubleading thermal corrections
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites the scalar crossing equation at high temperature so the real parts of zeta zeros determine correction exponents; RH fixes a common envelope, while an off-line zero generically changes it.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Recovering low zeta zeros from an SU(3)_1 scalar spectrum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Demonstrates how subtracting leading thermal terms and fitting log-periodic oscillations recovers early zeros, while explaining why finite spectral truncation tests only bounded height and is not new RH evidence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fixed-spin crossing and the return of Maass cusp forms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that nonzero-spin projection introduces sporadic Maass data absent in the scalar channel, even though the Eisenstein contour can still be evaluated and relates spin-j states to scalars.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Routes to stronger constraints beyond a single scalar equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares combining modular/four-point crossing, changing functional families, retaining zeta residues, and transporting the harmonic method to four-point functions or S-duality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Spectral-gap cancellation determines the allowed contour poles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Takes an inverse Laplace transform, uses discreteness and the vacuum gap to force cancellation of small-Δ power laws, and concludes that only the main pole and poles induced by zeta zeros can be crossed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Inversion-antisymmetric form of the scalar sum rule
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Recognizes that applying k^{3/2}∂_k exposes antisymmetry under k↔k^{-1}, producing an equivalent formulation valid for all c and identifying the vacuum as the Δ→0 limit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The c=1 crossing equation and cancellation of the ζ(1) divergence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Treats the divergent-average exception, checks the equation at arbitrary free-boson radius, and shows how a zero of the Mellin factor cancels the apparent ζ(1) divergence to yield a convergent general sum rule.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Regularized c=2 Eisenstein decomposition and zero-residue crossing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a finite-part Eisenstein series to handle c=2, derives the modified pole structure and rapidly convergent zero sum, and extends the result from Narain theories to general U(1)^2 CFTs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Heat flow turns RH into a threshold problem for real zeros

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Off-axis H_t asymptotics replace the missing t<0 Dirichlet series

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows the n=1 series term dominates, proves the huge-index tail negligible, compares t with zero, and uses holomorphy plus Borel-Caratheodory and Cauchy estimates to pass from modulus control to a logarithmic derivative estimate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Classical locations provide a nonuniform lattice for H_t zeros
