result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime tables suggest a local probability whose cumulative form is an integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gauss's empirical thinning heuristic replaces a count by a sum of local densities and then by Li(x), making the recurring sum-to-integral move explicit before stating the PNT scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH matters because it would turn Li(x) into a uniformly sharp prime-counting surrogate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The span distinguishes the PNT's first-order asymptotic from explicit two-sided estimates and the much sharper RH-conditional error, while noting that unavoidable prime irregularity rules out an even smaller proposed scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Complexifying the zeta variable transformed the prime-number problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source contrasts Euler's real-variable series with Riemann's analytic-function viewpoint and explains how later complex-function foundations converted the conceptual leap into the PNT proof tradition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An elementary PNT proof reproduces the theorem without reproducing Riemann's structural leverage
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Selberg's symmetry identity supports an elementary proof and extension to arithmetic progressions, but the survey records that hopes for broader new insight from avoiding complex analysis were not realized.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Continuation and completion expose the zeta function's reflection symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Two continuation devices lead to the meromorphic zeta function and its functional equation; multiplying by the polar factors produces the entire xi-function whose zeros are precisely the nontrivial zeta zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hadamard factorization and the functional equation organize zeros into fourfold symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The completed-function product turns zeros into factors, while functional-equation and conjugation symmetries reduce computation to one region and identify the critical line and finite-height RH certification target.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler products encode primes while explicit formulas reconstruct their count from zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Unique factorization becomes an Euler product, its singularity implies infinitely many primes, and Riemann's explicit formula expresses pi(x) as a smooth R(x) term corrected by every nontrivial zero; the table illustrates why R(x) improves Li(x).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic weights make the prime-zero correspondence analytically natural
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The von Mangoldt weight arises from logarithmically differentiating the Euler product, simplifies the explicit formula for psi(x), and makes the rightmost zero's real part control the prime-counting error, yielding an RH-equivalent error exponent.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Moving a zero-free boundary left improves prime errors, but known regions remain far from a power saving
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Von Koch's equivalence makes the critical-line location an error exponent, while explicit zero-free regions show how partial exclusion of zeros yields weaker PNT errors and expose the stubborn gap to any fixed x-to-a-power improvement.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Replacing prime probability by the average of Lambda leads naturally to psi, Pi, and R
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The average-one heuristic for the von Mangoldt function unifies equivalent PNT forms; counting prime powers and applying Möbius inversion then produces R(x) as a principled refinement of Li(x).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Numerical RH verification separates evaluation, localization, and completeness
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The rediscovery of Riemann's approximate formulas leads to a three-stage certification architecture: compute zeta accurately, locate critical-line zeros, and independently count all strip zeros up to the height so agreement has evidential force.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler-Maclaurin makes zeta computable with a certified but linearly growing cost
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A finite Dirichlet sum plus Bernoulli corrections and a controlled remainder gives prescribed-precision evaluation; the number of required terms grows linearly with the imaginary part, explaining why the simple method loses at height.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Hardy Z-function turns critical zeros into real sign changes sampled at Gram points
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Phase rotation makes critical-line zeta real, asymptotic phase monotonicity defines Gram points, and endpoint signs bracket zeros; empty intervals paired with neighboring double intervals show how the rule can fail locally without defeating computation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Argument variation counts all strip zeros but pointwise control of S(T) is fragile
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: N(T) and the argument term S(T) provide a total-zero count to compare with located critical zeros; Backlund's nearest-integer shortcut is obstructed by contour nonvanishing and unbounded S(T), and multiple zeros expose a separate failure mode.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positive proportions quantify progress without collapsing into full RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The historical chain from infinitely many critical zeros to a positive fraction and then successively improved constants provides a calibrated intermediate signal distinct from proving every zero critical.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riemann-Siegel replaces a length-t sum by a square-root-length oscillatory sum plus a controlled remainder
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Two evaluations of a contour integral produce the short cosine sum for Z(t); saddle-point analysis expands the remainder, and an explicit bound is what upgrades fast approximation into certified computation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Turing averages the counting discrepancy so any missed zeros create an impossible persistent bias
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replacing the unknown total count by the observed critical-zero count shifts S(t) downward by the number missed; an integral bound on S prevents that shift from persisting and yields a finite extra-height buffer for certification.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Fourier transform makes many nearby zeta evaluations cheaper than isolated evaluations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Odlyzko-Schoenhage maps an evenly sampled Dirichlet polynomial to rational-function values at roots of unity, so FFT-style batching changes the asymptotic cost of large zero-verification runs without improving a single evaluation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-verification records scale through algorithms and distributed computation but still require reproducible evidence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The chronological table and prose connect methodological advances to orders-of-magnitude growth and explicitly flag that two enormous computations were neither independently repeated nor published in a mathematical journal.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit formulas trade exhaustive prime enumeration for a finite certified zero input
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The evolution from combinatorial prime counting to Platt's unconditional explicit-formula computation shows how sufficiently accurate, complete critical-zero data can certify an exact pi(x) value far beyond direct enumeration.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Partial RH converts a verified zero range into explicit prime inequalities on a bounded x-range
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The span traces explicit bounds for pi, theta, and the nth prime to finite-height zero verification and states a direct relation between an RH height and the x-range on which an RH-strength inequality follows.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A tiny zero-driven oscillation can overturn an overwhelmingly persistent prime-counting bias
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The explicit formula explains why pi(x)-Li(x) must oscillate despite vast initial evidence, while accurately known zeros plus Lehman's bounds locate a region of reversed inequality and logarithmic density quantifies the remaining bias.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Mertens conjecture failed when an explicit zero sum was phase-aligned by Diophantine optimization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The reciprocal-zeta representation gives RH and PNT equivalences for M(x), a random-walk heuristic already warns against the square-root bound, and the disproof combines a truncated zero formula, certified roots and simplicity, simultaneous phase alignment, and LLL.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Ternary Goldbach closes by combining arc estimates with certified Dirichlet-L zero ranges
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The progression from GRH-conditional asymptotics through explicit bounds to Helfgott's unconditional proof shows computation serving as a bounded verification component inside a proof whose large range is handled analytically.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dirichlet series regularize erratic arithmetic data and contour shifting returns information to sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source abstracts a reusable Riemann reflex: encode an arithmetic function in a Dirichlet series, recover its summatory function by Perron's integral, shift the contour using continuation, and if necessary replace the function by a better-behaved proxy before transferring conclusions back.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The zeta template generalizes through a package of series, growth, continuation, reflection, and Euler factors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Dirichlet and Dedekind examples show how prime-distribution questions migrate to L-functions; the five listed Selberg-style properties separate the reusable architecture from the Riemann zeta function's particular coefficients.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rescaling zeros to unit mean spacing reveals repulsion through pair correlation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The N(T) asymptotic motivates unfolding the ordinates, Montgomery's pair statistic predicts suppressed near-collisions, and both a smooth theorem and Odlyzko's data connect the statistic to zero simplicity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Random Hermitian spectra supply a statistical model for zeta zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Dyson's recognition transfers Montgomery's zero-spacing law to a random-matrix ensemble, providing a model that generates otherwise inaccessible conjectures and makes high-height numerical checks scientifically important.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Random matrices predict the full hierarchy of zeta moments and are calibrated by known cases
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Known first and second moments establish anchors, matrix size near log(T/2pi) supplies the translation, and Keating-Snaith values extend the coefficient pattern to all moments while analytic special cases and high-zero computations test the dictionary.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Function fields turn parts of the random-matrix dictionary into theorems
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A structurally related setting where RH is known lets Katz-Sarnak prove random-matrix predictions, offering exact analogue evidence without transferring those proofs automatically to number fields.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Iterated logarithms can make divergent behavior look bounded on every feasible computation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The warning explains a concrete mechanism behind false computational conjectures: asymptotically unbounded functions such as iterated logarithms can remain visually flat, so numerics need theoretical or heuristic support.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite Euler products and independent prime phases create dense function-space orbits
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Mean approximation by truncated Euler products combines with rational independence of prime logarithms and Kronecker-Weyl phase control; Mergelyan and rearrangement tools complete target approximation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Value density becomes universality in a holomorphic function space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The progression from scalar values through derivative tuples to function-space density clarifies the conceptual lift, while Bagchi's functional limit theorem supplies a probabilistic proof route.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Second moments replace an unavailable prime-coefficient first moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For automorphic L-functions the positive-density method combines the classical prime harmonic sum with a proved coefficient second moment; higher moments can also remove Ramanujan-type assumptions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A prime geodesic theorem substitutes for the prime number theorem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Primitive-geodesic counting occupies the prime-counting role for Selberg zeta, and its error exponent directly limits the universality strip.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Joint universality turns analytic independence into orthogonality or matrix rank
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Character orthogonality, full-rank prime-class matrices, arithmetic-progression coefficient means, and Selberg orthogonality are compared, with counterexamples to an overweak criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Removing Euler-product constraints permits zero-bearing targets and creates many zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Hurwitz frequency independence or reduction to joint Dirichlet L-functions removes target nonvanishing; approximating a linear target and applying Rouche transfers one target zero to linearly many source zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Continuation alone cannot characterize universal Dirichlet series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A general theorem jointly requires independent exponents, continuation, growth, mean square, counting, and coefficient energy; a powers-of-two series refutes the continuation-only conjecture.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic independence removes matrix conditions but functional relations still obstruct joint universality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The progression toward direct independence of all logarithmic frequencies gives an intrinsic sufficient condition, while inversion identities and non-dense constructions show that individually universal functions need not be jointly universal.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One universal function yields a joint family on disjoint translated domains
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separate targets are pasted on disjoint translated compacta, converting single-function universality into joint universality without new coefficient independence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Recursive nonvanishing gates multiple zeta universality while mixed families need combined frequency independence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Multiple Hurwitz universality in the first variable depends on a lower-depth nonzero value; mixed universality instead combines prime and shifted-integer logarithms in one independence statement.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Self-approximation of zeta is equivalent to RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Zero density rules out strong universality for zeta, but zero-freeness lets ordinary universality target zeta itself; Bagchi's converse makes this recurrence equivalent to RH, while generalized ratios expose arithmetic exceptions and a documented gap.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A weighted ergodic average can replace uniform time density
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: If a weight preserves the Birkhoff-Khinchin expectation asymptotically, Bagchi's proof yields weighted universality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Discrete sampling adds a frequency that can force deletion of resonant Euler factors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The arithmetic nature of the step changes logarithmic independence and can require a modified L-function; the source explicitly corrects a published statement that ignored this.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Varying characters replaces vertical translation as the approximation parameter
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Character/discriminant variation creates dense L-value families, with real-axis symmetry constraining targets and class-number formulas transferring density to algebraic invariants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Derivative-value density forbids nontrivial continuous differential relations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Density of derivative tuples forces all coefficient functions in a universal identity to vanish; polynomial specialization gives differential algebraic independence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rearrangement and translation orbits unify classical and zeta universality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Fekete, Birkhoff, Riemann rearrangement, Pecherskii, Voronin, and Kronecker-Weyl fit one topological orbit framework while preserving the target subset distinction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Simultaneous torus control makes algebraic combinations strongly universal
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Prescribing auxiliary phases handles products and Dirichlet-series coefficients, yielding strong universality and linear zero counts for sums and polynomials of L-functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Ineffective rearrangement is the bottleneck in quantitative universality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The section compares convex separation plus quantitative Weyl, explicit small-domain estimates, functional-limit rates, and finite derivative approximation as routes from existence to bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Preimages and local Holder control transfer universality through an operator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Composite universality reduces to zero-free preimages for polynomial targets and continuity control, covering derivatives and nonlinear functions; a differential-equation method supplies an alternative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Universality persists under ergodic iterates and certain random paths
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Existence of a simultaneous approximating shift is equated with almost-sure ergodic recurrence and positive lower discrete density; random walks and Brownian motion extend the sampling interface.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Canonical semi-local operators motivate reopening an analytic route to Weil positivity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The introduction distinguishes an artificial global spectral realization from canonical finite-place operators, identifies normalization as the likely missing ingredient in a failed local argument, and bounds the paper's analytic proposal against the established geometric program.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The symmetrized PQ Hamiltonian is exactly the generator of unitary scaling
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source removes a supposed quantization mystery by identifying P and Q in the Heisenberg representation, showing that one-half(PQ+QP) generates scaling, while its unboundedness explains the absence of a discrete spectrum without cutoffs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A symplectic cutoff comparison makes absorption and emission counts agree but preserves a quantum sign
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A symplectic map identifies the white-light phase space with the multiplicative scaling picture; subtracting it leaves the Berry-Keating region, so semiclassical counts agree, yet the absorption minus sign reappears in Maslov phases and prevents model equivalence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Commutators with a Hilbert-transform involution form a differential calculus
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replacing ordinary differentiation by [F,f] yields a graded differential squaring to zero; in one variable the commutator kernel becomes a divided difference, and the construction extends to arbitrary modulated abelian groups.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite sets of places produce canonical adèle-class approximations with compatible Fourier and scaling actions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Quotienting the finite product A_S by its S-units defines X_S, removes the global measure singularity, and yields a Hilbert space where additive Fourier transform, multiplicative scaling, and local L-factor ratios coexist canonically.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Infrared and Fourier-dual cutoffs turn the scaling trace into a sum of local explicit-formula terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The product of physical and Fourier cutoffs is conjugated to interval projections and the quantized differential of the local-factor ratio; additivity of the logarithmic derivative then decomposes its trace place by place and yields the semi-local trace formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Li's positive-operator strategy succeeds exactly when a local-factor ratio is inner
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proposed small-q/small-p cutoff would turn Weil negativity into positivity of a trace-class product, but Lemma 3.4 proves this is equivalent to invariance of a Hardy subspace, hence to an inner-function condition on the unitary local multiplier.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local factor ratios have unit boundary modulus without Hardy boundedness
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Both finite-prime and archimedean ratios are holomorphic on the relevant right half-plane yet unbounded, so they are not inner; moreover the desired inequality would force monotonicity of the Riemann-Siegel phase, which its graph contradicts.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Compact support localizes Weil positivity to finitely many places
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Weil's criterion is translated into negativity for convolution-square test functions with two vanishing moments, leading to the conjecture that primes below q plus the archimedean place suffice for support inside (q to minus one-half, q to one-half).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson summation conjugates Fourier inversion and forces the local-factor ratio
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The map summing scaled copies becomes multiplication by zeta under Mellin transform; Poisson summation identifies additive Fourier transform with inversion, so their multiplier is the quotient of zeta boundary values and hence the archimedean local-factor ratio, with the same mechanism surviving semi-locally.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Fourier-compatible scaling differential turns the Poisson distribution into Sonine functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applying a differential operator whose range has zero value and zero Fourier value to the self-dual Poisson distribution creates simultaneous support gaps; smoothing then yields Schwartz Sonine functions, and the symmetric operator is built from the scaling generator.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Function-field zeros are naturally periodic times rather than energy levels
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For curves over finite fields, zeta is a rational function of q to minus s and numerator roots lie on a circle, making imaginary parts repeat modulo 2 pi over log q; this periodicity favors the dual time interpretation of zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The analytic route is normalization-sensitive while geometry supplies global conceptual structure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The conclusion keeps the semi-local operator conjecture alive but emphasizes that principal-value choices make an analytic proof fragile, whereas the global Scaling Site interprets scaling as Frobenius and exposes structure absent semi-locally.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The semiclassical limit becomes a high-eigenvalue problem for geodesic flow
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Quantizing the geodesic Hamiltonian identifies h→0 with Laplace eigenvalue growth and turns correspondence with classical dynamics into concrete questions about eigenvalues and eigenfunctions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Invariant tori and stable orbits localize modes, while unstable orbits pose the chaotic problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source contrasts Bohr-Sommerfeld torus localization and whispering-gallery modes with negative-curvature chaos, then shows how a stable periodic orbit creates both an eigenvalue progression and localized quasimodes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quantum ergodicity controls density-one subsequences but not individual scarred limits
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Quantum ergodicity yields equidistribution for almost all modes and invariance for any quantum limit, while leaving exceptional localization open; the random-wave model supplies stronger distributional and sup-norm predictions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Number variance distinguishes Poisson spectra from GOE and GUE rigidity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After unfolding to unit mean spacing, number variance gives a common statistic for Poisson and random-matrix models and motivates the universality claim that integrable systems are Poissonian while generic chaotic systems are rigid.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Persistent strong scarring is a measure-limit claim, not a finite-energy enhancement
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Numerical stadium states motivate a distinction between visible finite-energy scars and strong scarring defined by singular support of a limiting eigenfunction measure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hyperbolic quotients supply chaotic systems with computable arithmetic structure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constant-negative-curvature surfaces are represented as discrete group quotients, with arithmetic examples including the modular surface where cusp forms coexist with continuous Eisenstein spectrum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Modular eigenfunctions exhibit Gaussian local amplitudes without visible localization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The checked prose reports Gaussian distribution functions for high modular cusp forms and states a concrete random-wave conjecture for their amplitude distributions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Observed spectral simplicity becomes an input to later deformation results
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: High computations suggest the even modular spectrum is simple, and the source flags this conjecture as consequential rather than merely descriptive.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic hyperbolic spectra are Poisson-like while nonarithmetic peers follow GOE
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Takeuchi's trace characterization separates arithmetic lattices, and numerical number variance then reveals the central exception: chaotic arithmetic surfaces behave spectrally like integrable systems.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Measure-zero families of periodic trajectories can force macroscopic spectral variance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A clean fixed-point family in the geodesic flow produces a lower bound for the averaged Weyl remainder, explaining why bouncing-ball families dominate beyond the universal range.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic length clustering drives spectral nonrigidity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lower bounds for number variance are traced to high multiplicity and bounded clustering of arithmetic geodesic lengths, while the absence of upper bounds is explicitly identified.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hecke correspondences create commuting nonlocal probes exactly in the arithmetic case
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Finite correspondences on a quotient define operators commuting with the Laplacian, and Margulis's commensurator dichotomy explains why arithmetic manifolds carry an infinite supply of such probes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hecke symmetry rules out strong geodesic scarring and motivates QUE
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The no-scarring theorem eliminates quantum limits singular on finitely many geodesic submanifolds for congruence Hecke eigenbases, and QUE strengthens this to individual equidistribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sup-norm growth is framed as an eigenfunction analogue of Lindelöf and Ramanujan
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Local universal bounds are separated from the conjectural negative-curvature bound; arithmetic amplification improves convexity, produces rare large values, and links sup norms to zeta and automorphic L-function growth.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Theta lifts create singular arithmetic eigenfunctions in dimension three
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An infinite subsequence violates random-wave size predictions because most eigenfunctions vanish at a special arithmetic point, forcing the surviving modes to be large there.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Special L-value nonvanishing dissolves cusp forms under nonarithmetic deformation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The existence of bound states is tied to arithmeticity through a Fermi-golden-rule condition expressed by Rankin-Selberg L-values, with spectral simplicity or multiplicity control governing generic finiteness results.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Random-matrix philosophy moves from Laplace levels to Hecke spectra
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Although Laplace spectra on arithmetic surfaces evade GOE, Hecke operators recover semicircle and Ramanujan phenomena and yield explicit graphs mimicking random regular graphs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional equations give convexity while Euler products motivate RH and Lindelöf
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The section builds from zeta to higher-degree Euler products, separates analytic continuation and functional equation from Euler-product input, and organizes RH, Lindelöf, convexity, and subconvexity as distinct levels.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Eisenstein series turn L-function bounds into testable eigenfunction bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Fourier expansion identifies zeta factors inside generalized eigenfunctions, while cusp truncation supplies an effective local L2 normalization so eigenfunction conjectures can be tested on continuous spectrum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A CM-point value converts the sup-norm conjecture into Lindelöf for a Dedekind zeta function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Evaluating an Eisenstein series at an arithmetic point factors it into zeta and a Dirichlet L-function, so a geometric pointwise bound implies critical-line growth control for a degree-two zeta function and then for Riemann zeta.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Cusp-form values at arithmetic points encode central twisted L-values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shimura-Waldspurger type identities and Fourier-coefficient normalization make the pointwise sup-norm problem equivalent to Lindelöf in the spectral aspect for a degree-two automorphic L-function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rankin-Selberg subconvexity controls individual mass equidistribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An integral representation of a degree-four Rankin-Selberg L-function turns mass against Eisenstein tests into central values; beating convexity in the spectral aspect would already imply individual equidistribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A clean periodic fixed set forces an averaged Weyl remainder through a trace singularity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Duistermaat-Guillemin trace formula creates a nonzero oscillatory term, and a calculus lemma transfers its smoothed size into an L1 and then L2 lower bound for the counting remainder.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Selberg's trace formula turns clustered geodesic lengths into number-variance lower bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A smoothed spectral increment becomes a Dirichlet polynomial over closed geodesics; bounded trace clustering controls the mean square, while geodesic multiplicities make the diagonal large enough to force nonrigidity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Hecke correspondence transports singular mass to an isolated preimage and yields a contradiction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An algebraic separation lemma chooses a correspondence meeting the alleged singular support once; the Hecke eigenrelation and Cauchy inequality then force zero mass in a neighborhood that must carry singular support.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hecke weights break the local sup-norm barrier
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The pre-trace formula gives only a local convexity-scale bound; applying Hecke operators, counting near-fixed arithmetic correspondences, and choosing amplifier coefficients isolates one eigenfunction and improves that bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: CM points fixed by many correspondences force exceptional eigenfunction values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A different positive pre-trace kernel and a product of split primes create an arithmetic coefficient substantially larger at CM points than the generic bound, producing infinitely many large eigenfunctions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic structure explains both exceptional spectral statistics and unusually strong proof methods
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The conclusion separates the dimension-two random-wave picture, dimension-three theta-lift failures, Poisson-like arithmetic level statistics, and the methodological limitation that current progress relies on correspondences rather than dynamics.

section_argument_map.label: 3. Arithmetic manifolds
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Explains arithmetic spectral nonrigidity, Hecke correspondences, scarring obstructions, QUE, sup norms, theta-lift exceptions, and bound-state arithmeticity.

section_argument_map.label: 4. L-functions
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Connects zeta and automorphic L-function growth to Eisenstein and cusp-form sup norms and to quantum unique ergodicity via Rankin-Selberg values.

section_argument_map.label: 5. Outline of some proofs
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses trace formulas, arithmetic clustering, Hecke separation, and amplified pre-trace inequalities to justify the principal spectral and eigenfunction results.

section_argument_map.label: 6. Conclusion and acknowledgements
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Synthesizes the arithmetic exceptions and identifies the need for dynamical replacements for arithmetic methods.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Harmonic families arise by isolating spectra and applying an L-group representation, while geometric families specialize a smooth proper scheme and invoke modularity; the comparison cleanly separates parameter space from the resulting automorphic image.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite-to-one conductor ordering makes local coefficient averages into family densities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source makes infinitude and finite counting structural requirements, then states a quantitative vertical limit whose main terms can be interpreted prime by prime and whose uniform error controls later zero statistics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Three trace moments decompose a family into unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic mass
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Conjecture 1 lifts vertical p-adic equidistribution to a family Sato-Tate measure; three compact-group indicators then recover cuspidality, self-duality, and Frobenius-Schur sign and determine the unique type proportions even when the underlying group decomposition is nonunique.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Persistent central zeros and functional-equation parity require independent family refinements
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The rank is encoded in the next term of local coefficient convergence and is removed before studying fluctuations, whereas the symplectic root-number split depends on ramified local signs and Mobius cancellation; neither is determined by the leading Sato-Tate measure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Homogeneity type reverses into the low-zero random-matrix symmetry class
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After conductor scaling, the universality conjecture maps unitary families to unitary statistics, orthogonal families to symplectic statistics, and symplectic sign subfamilies to even or odd orthogonal statistics, while explicitly omitting forced central zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic characters calibrate the entire family-to-density interface
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The quadratic family has an explicit product local measure and symplectic low-zero prediction; restricted-support theorems and a function-field comparison show how matching finite-field densities can certify otherwise difficult combinatorial identities over the rationals.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Generic specialization transfers a finite Galois representation into a family Sato-Tate law
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Hilbert irreducibility supplies generic fibers with fixed Galois group, finite-field point counting supplies vertical limits, and geometry-of-numbers orbit parametrizations turn cubic through quintic fields into conductor-ordered families whose symmetry is read from the standard symmetric-group representation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Height, generic rank, and average root number probe different mechanisms in elliptic families
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Monodromy fixes the leading symplectic type, the Tate conjecture connects the family rank to an elliptic surface, and multiplicative-fiber polynomials govern average root signs; explicit examples show rank and root number can vary independently.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dwork parity changes the monodromy pairing and therefore the predicted zero symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An invariant cohomological summand gives a fixed-degree automorphic family; even n yields full symplectic monodromy and a mixture of orthogonal zero laws, while odd n yields orthogonal monodromy and symplectic zero statistics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The identity orbital term creates Plancherel mass and all other orbits control the error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Quantitative trace-formula equidistribution identifies each local family measure as a functorial pushforward of Plancherel measure; uniform control of nonidentity orbital integrals is exactly what makes the prime and family parameters usable together.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An irreducible L-group representation determines harmonic homogeneity and forces rank zero
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Macdonald's Plancherel formula turns representation-theoretic irreducibility, self-duality, and pairing sign into the three family indicators and gives a smaller next-order coefficient that makes the harmonic rank vanish; the partial-L formulation also insulates low zeros from uncertain ramified factors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Petersson equidistribution separates modular forms by root sign before zero statistics can distinguish them
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The PGL(2) family has the classical SU(2) Sato-Tate measure and symplectic homogeneity; local Steinberg alternatives split root signs equally, and extending Fourier support beyond one is what separates even-orthogonal, odd-orthogonal, and symplectic one-level laws.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Twisting averages an individual Sato-Tate measure and can erase self-duality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Quadratic twists average a measure with its negative and retain the seed representation's pairing type, whereas all character twists add a full central circle, force both self-duality indicators to vanish, and yield unitary symmetry independently of the seed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Frobenius-Schur indicators multiply under products even when root signs alone do not explain symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A GL(2) by symmetric-square family has fixed even sign yet orthogonal-matrix zero statistics, and the general tensor-product rule predicts the product type by multiplying pairing indicators; adjoint families give a broad orthogonal-to-symplectic example.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Natural trace-formula weights can manufacture a misleading symmetry type
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The spin family of Siegel forms has a representation-theoretically fixed symplectic type, but central-value weights introduced by the available Petersson formula carry enough fluctuation to alter the observed density, isolating weighting as an evaluation confound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Universal conductor families can retain zero universality when local Sato-Tate limits fail
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Plancherel slices predict local measures for the universal family, yet irregular level sequences destroy the simple vertical limit while low-zero universality is still expected, separating the two conjectural channels.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reducing parameters modulo p turns local family statistics into a finite atomic measure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Good reduction makes the unramified conjugacy class depend only on the parameter modulo p, integer-point equidistribution converges to the uniform finite-field sum, and the discriminant locus has negligible mass, reducing the family problem to finite fields.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Geometric monodromy converts finite-field Frobenius samples into Haar Sato-Tate measure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The lisse cohomology sheaf supplies arithmetic and geometric monodromy groups, purity places normalized Frobenius in a compact group, and Deligne-Katz equidistribution makes its Haar pushforward the family Sato-Tate law.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Intersections of benign families can encode arbitrary Diophantine sets and lose all statistics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Allowing a general integral base or forming an intersection introduces an unrestricted Diophantine parameter set; a recursive-set construction shows that even basic counting limits can then fail, justifying the deliberately narrow family definition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bounding fields of rationality may secretly select geometric families or finite sets
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source relates rational-coefficient weight-two forms to elliptic curves, proposes higher-weight Calabi-Yau realizations, and shows that infinitude is a substantive gate; rationality-bounded spectral subsets cannot simply be treated as ordinary harmonic families.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Plancherel-null local condition defeats the trace formula before symmetry can be tested
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Fixing a cohomological or algebraic archimedean component may define a natural family, but zero Plancherel mass makes even its conductor count hard and removes the isolation mechanism used for harmonic equidistribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Specifying an H-type is conceptually natural but analytically circular
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A universal type family would require both defining the individual group and recognizing its members, problems as hard as individual Langlands classification; geometric specialization and class field theory yield tractable subfamilies without solving the universal problem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Automorphic induction combines varying fields with harmonic data beyond the basic formation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The construction varies number fields, applies an L-group representation over each, and induces back to the rationals, showing how geometric and spectral parameters can be composed while common L-factors and mixed Galois types require explicit handling.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weil-Deligne representations make ramified geometric local factors comparable to automorphic ones
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The appendix defines conductor and local L-factor from inertia and monodromy, assembles them for algebraic l-adic representations, and formulates geometry as a cohomological source, providing the exact interface used by geometric families.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Modularity matches geometric Galois data to automorphic data and the weight twist restores unitarity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The two conjectural formulations distinguish existence of an automorphic realization from a bijective algebraic correspondence with local-global compatibility; Deligne weights explain the precise twist making good-reduction local components unitary and identify weight-monodromy as the bad-reduction gate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A critical center would force a symplectic pairing, excluding regular algebraic orthogonal forms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under the stated motivic correspondences, parity of the motivic weight first restricts criticality to even rank and a sign theorem then makes the l-adic pairing symplectic, contradicting orthogonal type; the examples distinguish Dirichlet and elliptic behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Convexity as a reusable fractional-moment move

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic truncation and Gaussian log-values predict the same moment exponent
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the k^2 logarithmic exponent from two distinct representations: divisor-coefficient diagonal sums and a Gaussian model for log|ζ|, while isolating an arithmetic Euler factor from an unknown global factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Keating-Snaith's full moment constant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States a uniform positive-real-k conjecture whose constant factors through the Barnes G-function and specializes to explicit integer combinatorics.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains the transfer from GUE/CUE zero statistics to characteristic-polynomial moments via N≈log(T/2π), identifies what random matrices recover, and notes that the arithmetic factor must be supplied or recovered by hybrid models.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Three fronts of progress toward the moment conjecture
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Cleanly separates RH-conditional high-moment upper bounds, unconditional small-moment upper bounds, and unconditional all-moment lower bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-polynomial upper bounds by adaptive scales and rare-event disposal
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Bounds log|ζ| by a prime sum under RH, partitions primes into scales, assigns smaller powers to larger-prime blocks, approximates exponentials on typical sets, and uses high moments plus Markov bounds to make exceptional sets negligible.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Twisted control at one moment propagates sharp upper bounds downward

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Twisted moments propagate sharp lower bounds upward and below the first moment

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hasse's first proof lifts to a convenient CM curve and counts division points after reduction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains how extension of the constants field, selection of a CM lattice and ring class field, and reduction of division points turn an elliptic pRH problem into explicit class-field theory, while recording the odd-degree restriction and the later Hasse bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Ordinary and supersingular elliptic curves are distinguished by p-torsion and endomorphism algebra
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Presents equivalent structural diagnostics for ordinary versus supersingular curves, identifies the quaternionic endomorphism case, and connects supersingular parameters to a polynomial and class-number count.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite-field endomorphisms generalize from elliptic CM to Honda-Tate classification
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how Deuring's elliptic results inspired Tate's CM statement for finite-field abelian varieties, distinguishes definition from descent, and classifies Frobenius/endomorphism behavior into ordinary and two supersingular cases.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Changing the ground field invalidates a claimed supersingularity converse
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Diagnoses Hasse's conflation of a curve over an algebraic closure with its chosen finite-field Frobenius, gives supersingular counterexamples away from endpoint traces, and uses Honda-Tate conditions to state which quadratic Weil numbers actually arise from elliptic curves.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Frobenius norm plus conjugating involution yields Hasse's second proof
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compresses the elliptic pRH proof into the identity between Frobenius and its conjugate and identifies the relevant anti-involution later called Rosati, replacing the first proof's lifting construction by intrinsic endomorphism structure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Higher genus forced a choice between analytic uniformization and structural algebra
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts Hasse's preference for a purely structural second proof with his initial proposal to generalize CM and abelian-function uniformization, then records Deuring's apparently decisive alternative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Replace elliptic endomorphisms by self-correspondences, but the norm generalization remains absent
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines Deuring's higher-genus move from an endomorphism ring to a ring of curve correspondences, algebraizes the construction in function-field language, and explicitly lists differential action and a generalized norm/positivity statement as the two missing components.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Equivalent correspondence ideas failed to combine across mathematical dialects
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Weil's response identifies pre-existing Italian algebraic geometry as a source of the same correspondence ring, while the later workshop and publications show how incompatible languages, attribution disputes, and war-era fragmentation blocked the hoped-for collective proof program.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Deuring completes elliptic CM lifting, but higher-dimensional lifting needs ordinarity or isogeny
result_and_mechanism_map.unit_type: lifting theorem and boundary of generalization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States lifting of an elliptic curve together with an endomorphism, explains why it repairs Hasse's first proof, and contrasts the elliptic theorem with nonliftable higher-dimensional pairs and the eventual isogeny-qualified CM lifting result.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Equivalent avatars prevent RH from belonging to one inherited discipline
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares special-functions, real-analysis, prime-distribution, and arithmetic-algebraic placements of classical RH and argues that historical classification is provisional until a proof reveals the structural root.

section_argument_map.label: Repository metadata, abstract, and contents
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Defines the historical interval, pRH subject, and scope while providing acquisition metadata.

section_argument_map.label: Introduction
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Frames history as evidence about where RH avatars belong and summarizes the Artin-Schmidt-Hasse-Weil sequence.

section_argument_map.label: 1 From Richard Dedekind to Emil Artin
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Traces the arithmetic/analytic inheritance, derives Artin's function-field zeta representation, formulates pRH as a root-modulus condition, and reviews finite computational cases.

section_argument_map.label: 2 Some formulas for zeta functions and pRH
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Defines scheme-style Euler products and point-count generating functions, gives rational curve zeta form, and translates pRH and point counts into Frobenius-root data.

section_argument_map.label: 3 F.K. Schmidt
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Replaces variable-dependent affine arithmetic with an intrinsic function-field framework and separates functional equation, rationality, and pRH.

section_argument_map.label: 4 The Last Entry
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Reinterprets Gauss's point-count observation as a CM elliptic-curve Frobenius statement and follows reduction from characteristic zero.

section_argument_map.label: 5 Hasse's first proof
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Explains the CM-lifting strategy, its extension-field maneuver, its technical restrictions, and the Hasse point-count bound.

section_argument_map.label: 6 Elliptic curves
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Surveys ordinary/supersingular endomorphism structure, CM and Honda-Tate classification, and uses counterexamples to expose errors caused by changing ground fields.

section_argument_map.label: 7 Hasse's second proof
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Expresses pRH through Frobenius norm and the conjugating involution intrinsic to the endomorphism algebra.

section_argument_map.label: 8 Rational points over a field
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Adjacent digression contrasting rational-point existence over finite fields with genus-one obstructions over other fields.

section_argument_map.label: 9 Deuring's idea and its reception
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Documents the move to higher-genus correspondences, the missing positivity/norm ingredients, and competing function-field versus algebraic-geometric languages.

section_argument_map.label: 10 The Deuring lifting theorem
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: States lifting of an elliptic curve with an endomorphism and maps precisely how higher-dimensional lifting requires ordinarity or passage to an isogenous variety.

section_argument_map.label: 11 Reflections on the place of classical RH
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses disciplinary history and equivalent avatars to argue that RH's eventual mathematical location remains unsettled until a proof supplies its structural roots.

section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Bibliography only.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Real and imaginary level sets form an X-ray of a meromorphic function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces a representation in which crossings are zeros or poles and the global network organizes otherwise scattered information about zeta.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Branch crossings and monotonicity distinguish zeros from derivative zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that real/imaginary branches meet at zeros and poles, while same-type branches meet where the derivative vanishes; away from critical points, the relevant real or imaginary value changes monotonically along a branch.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integer line labels preserve branch identity through turns and mergers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines a parity-sensitive naming scheme tied to trivial zeros and intervening real branches, permitting later statements about sheets, crossings, and branch counts without relying only on position.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The first Dirichlet term creates parallel branches with alternating zero behavior
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses uniform convergence to one and dominance of the n=2 term to predict horizontal real-valued branches separated by pi/log 2; monotonic orientation explains why alternating branches must pass through zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Curve orientation turns each complementary region into a value quadrant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the sign of monotone motion on boundary branches to orient crossings and assigns every connected region to one quadrant of the zeta-value plane.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Boundary traversal counts solutions of zeta(s)=a inside a level-set region
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Maps a region boundary into quadrant-axis arcs, reads its winding number, and obtains an exact count of value preimages; the same geometry forces an interior derivative zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Numerical branch continuation is not uniformly certified near the critical strip
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Documents the root-localization and curve-ordering workflow and explicitly says paths far from the strip were proved while near-strip paths were followed until visually convincing and therefore are not proofs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Line-number growth becomes the classical zero-count asymptotic
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the functional equation to label branches on the left, then applies the argument principle to a boundary made from level curves and vertical segments, converting the label into the count of nontrivial zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riemann-Siegel trades generality for square-root-length critical-line evaluation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts arbitrary-precision Euler-Maclaurin evaluation with Hardy's real-valued normalization and the much shorter Riemann-Siegel sum, explaining why sign changes efficiently locate critical-line zeros at large height.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Branch-count imbalance forces most left branches to close into sheets
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares O(log t) crossings available in a horizontal critical-strip segment with order t log t branches arriving from the left, forcing pairwise returns called sheets and revealing nested behavior at larger heights.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Derivative zeros reconnect monotone branches while every non-polar branch escapes compact sets
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains how to continue a monotone level curve through a derivative zero by switching among equally many increasing and decreasing arms and records the global no-compact-endpoint property.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH is equivalent to every real sheet meeting the critical line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Each sheet contains exactly one zero by monotonicity. Hardy-phase orientation at critical-line crossings then distinguishes sheets whose zero lies on, right of, or left of the line, yielding the geometric RH criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gram points provide a phase-defined mesh that usually brackets critical-line zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines Gram points by Hardy's phase, derives that zeta is real there, and relates the typical sign pattern to alternating signs of Z(t), giving a computational zero-separation method and a route to infinitely many critical-line zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A left derivative zero and a left zeta zero force each other geometrically
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Presents Speiser's criterion that RH is equivalent to nontrivial derivative zeros lying on or right of the critical line, using constant-argument paths and monotonic modulus to construct the opposite kind of zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Derivative zeros govern branch attraction and the asymptotic number of sheets
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Interprets near-right-angle branch behavior through nearby derivative zeros and combines counts of parallel non-sheet zeros with total zero count to recover the asymptotic count of derivative zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Failures of Gram's law preserve total count through neighboring empty and double intervals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the first failure to show that interval-by-interval zero separation is too rigid, then reframes the more stable correspondence as a sheet pairing between Gram points and zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Lehmer pair is a near-reconnection that would move two zeros off the line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects two extremely close critical-line zeros and a tiny intervening Hardy maximum to abrupt level-curve turns and a nearby derivative zero; a small alternative reconnection would create a symmetric off-line pair.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: S(t) measures when Gram and Rosser regularities must fail
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines Gram blocks and Rosser's block-count rule, then interprets S(t) as horizontal level-curve crossings: thresholds near one and two explain failure of Gram's and Rosser's laws, while Selberg's omega result forces unbounded future complexity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Large values of S(t) predict coils involving arbitrarily many level curves
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines a second Rosser counterexample with unbounded S(t) to predict higher coils of increasing branch multiplicity and notes that real-part level curves can penetrate well right of one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Regular X-rays also arise from special-function structure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares zeta's level-set representation with Hermite, Bessel, Airy, and Gamma examples, showing that visually regular branch networks can follow special polynomial or differential-function structure and are not unique evidence of zeta arithmetic.

section_argument_map.label: 2.3 Right of the critical strip

section_argument_map.label: 2.4-2.5 Orientation and regions
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Orients level curves by monotonicity and maps complementary regions to value quadrants.

section_argument_map.label: 2.6 The equation zeta(s)=a
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses winding of a region boundary to count value preimages and infer derivative zeros.

section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Records numerical construction and explicitly separates proved outer-plane paths from manually followed near-strip curves.

section_argument_map.label: 2.8 Existence and count of nontrivial zeros
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Relates branch labels to zero counts through the functional equation and argument principle.

section_argument_map.label: 3. Computational techniques
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Compares Euler-Maclaurin and Riemann-Siegel evaluation and explains sign-based detection of critical-line zeros.

section_argument_map.label: 4. Critical-strip graphics
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses global branch topology to motivate sheets, line-count growth, and nested behavior; most intervening pages are extracted figure labels.

section_argument_map.label: 5. First Speiser theorem
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Equates RH with every real-valued sheet meeting the critical line.

section_argument_map.label: 6. Gram points
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Defines Gram points via Hardy's phase and explains their usual sign alternation and zero-separation role.

section_argument_map.label: 7. Second Speiser theorem
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Gives a caveated geometric derivation of the derivative-zero criterion and connects sheets to the count of derivative zeros.

section_argument_map.label: 8. Counterexample to Gram's law
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Shows how adjacent empty/double Gram intervals preserve total count and replaces interval pairing by sheet pairing.

section_argument_map.label: 9. Lehmer's almost counterexample
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Interprets a close zero pair and tiny Hardy-function maximum as a near-topological reconnection controlled by a derivative zero.

section_argument_map.label: 10. Rosser's law and S(t)
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Defines Gram blocks and S(t), visualizes the first Rosser failures, and predicts arbitrarily complex coils from unbounded S(t).

section_argument_map.label: Comparison functions
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Image-heavy zeta panels followed by X-rays of Hermite, Bessel, Airy, and Gamma functions that stress-test which visual regularities are zeta-specific.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Nonvanishing at Re(s)=1 becomes the prime number theorem through a Tauberian bridge
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The section separates the analytic input from the arithmetic output and identifies Tauberian theory as the conceptual mediator, while contrasting complex-analytic and elementary proofs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The explicit formula requires rho log x rather than the ambiguous symbol x^rho
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source diagnoses a genuine representation error, restores von Mangoldt's single-valued exponential-integral variable, and then places primes and zeros on opposite sides of the Guinand-Weil test-function formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gaussian averaging makes a remote prime-counting sign change detectable
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The historical progression isolates smoothing by a Gaussian kernel as the mechanism that converts an oscillatory explicit formula into effective sign-change bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Real-valued Z and mollification turn cancellation into lower bounds for critical-line zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Hardy's phase normalization makes sign changes visible, while Selberg and later mollifiers convert averaged inverse-zeta cancellation into positive-proportion results.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-free regions, zero density, and Lindelof encode progressively different controls
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The section distinguishes exclusion of zeros near one, density control inside the strip, and convex growth control on vertical lines instead of collapsing them into a single approximation to RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Evenness cancels Hadamard exponential factors in the Xi product
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Passing from xi to the even Xi function pairs zeros and removes the canonical-product exponentials, exposing a representation in factors of 1-s squared over alpha squared.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero alignment is exceptional and unstable under nonzero value perturbations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Nevanlinna/Jensen growth language and the Borchsenius-Jessen theorem show that zeros of zeta minus a nonzero constant crowd the right of the critical line, sharply separating the value zero from generic values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hilbert-space rearrangement turns prime Euler factors into universality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A square-summable but directionally divergent sequence has dense unimodular sums; applied to logarithms of Euler factors, this supplies the approximation engine behind Voronin universality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Self-adjoint spectra would force RH, but proposed operators lack a complete construction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Hilbert-Polya and scattering viewpoints translate critical-line zeros into real spectral data while recording that boundary conditions and rigorous operator realizations remain elusive.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Function-field RH becomes a positivity statement on geometry and Frobenius cohomology
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Weil's intersection pairing and the later etale-cohomological determinant representation show how zero location follows from geometric positivity and weight bounds, motivating but not supplying an arithmetic analogue for Spec Z.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adeles unify global arithmetic, while a sign separates Selberg spectra from zeta absorption
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source connects global fields to locally compact adelic companions, automorphic L-functions, and the Selberg trace formula, then identifies the opposite sign of prime terms as a structural obstacle to a direct spectral imitation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: GUE agreement requires height-dependent unfolding and is therefore intrinsically local
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Pair correlation and computations support GUE statistics only after rescaling by the changing zero density; that necessary unfolding rules out interpreting the match as a fixed finite-density operator without further structure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Katz-Sarnak assigns matrix symmetry by L-function family and proves the finite-field model
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The family viewpoint moves beyond one zeta function: arithmetic structure selects unitary, orthogonal, or symplectic statistics, with Frobenius and equidistribution making the finite-field case rigorous.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta moment constants split into universal random-matrix and arithmetic Euler factors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Keating-Snaith model isolates a universal characteristic-polynomial factor from a family-specific Euler product, a reusable pattern for transferring statistical structure without erasing arithmetic data.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The adele-class quotient realizes zeros as an absorption spectrum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Encoding the ergodic quotient by a crossed-product algebra produces a trace formula whose minus sign is explained by absorption rather than ordinary eigenvalues; periodic prime orbits then acquire a class-field-theoretic interpretation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riemann-Siegel evaluation plus Turing counting separates computed zeros from certified completeness
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The computational history identifies the methodological pair needed for rigorous verification: fast evaluation locates candidates while the Turing method checks that none were missed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Compact support turns global RH into Weil positivity involving finitely many primes at a time
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The explicit formula yields a quadratic-form criterion equivalent to RH, while support of the test function cuts off all but finitely many local prime terms; the source also notes that numerically proved archimedean positivity lacks a mechanism known to survive adding primes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH can be recast as density, coefficient positivity, or divisor-sum inequalities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Beurling-Nyman, Li, Robin, and Lagarias translate zero location into distinct functional-analytic, zero-sum, and elementary-arithmetic representations, illustrating both transfer opportunities and representation-specific costs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An elementary universal criterion can remain computationally unusable
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The discussion distinguishes logical equivalence from feasible verification: factorization and unbounded universal quantification prevent direct checking from becoming a proof strategy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Single-valued Ei of rho log x repairs the traditional statement of Riemann's formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The letter derives the failure of Li(x to rho) notation from its periodic loss of rho information and shows why the unexponentiated variable restores a meaningful conditional zero sum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A constrained Weil-form minimizer from finitely many primes produces a transform with line-constrained zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compact support makes the quadratic form computable from finitely many prime powers; existence and a simplicity-evenness condition give an extremizer whose Mellin zeros lie on the critical line, while numerical agreement suggests but does not prove convergence to zeta zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A simple even ground state of a translation-kernel quadratic form has a real-zero Fourier transform
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 6.1 supplies the abstract real-zero engine for every finite support scale and explains the finite-matrix self-adjoint approximation and Hurwitz limit used in computation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riemann's Xi kernel is a summation image of a two-Hermite combination
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Poisson symmetry and the summation map E convert Xi into the Fourier transform of the unique integral-zero combination of the zeroth and fourth Hermite modes, giving a finite-mode target for localization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prolate eigenfunctions diagonalize the near intersection of time and frequency windows
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The commuting prolate differential operator turns two noncommuting projections into a common spectral problem, with exponentially near-one eigenvalues quantifying functions that are almost both time- and band-limited.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson duality converts prolate near-intersection into a near-null vector of the restricted Weil form
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replacing Hermite modes by localized prolate modes and applying E yields a compactly supported vector; the impossibility of exact simultaneous support explains why it is only near the global radical and why its Weil value is extremely small.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The prolate candidate converges to Xi, but identification with the true Weil minimizer remains open
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source proves uniform convergence of the candidate transforms on closed substrips, then isolates two missing facts: simplicity/evenness of the restricted Weil ground state and a strong comparison between the candidate and that state.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Time and frequency projections rewrite the archimedean explicit formula as a trace identity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Scaling kernels translate geometric correspondences into operators; the two-cutoff trace formula then exposes the same projections as communication theory, with the Sonin complement providing a positive contribution to the Weil form.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Semilocal adele quotients add finitely many prime orbits to the time-frequency trace formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Crossed-product sheaves encode the quotient geometry compatibly with Spec Z, and the semilocal trace formula extends the archimedean projection identity by exactly the selected finite set of prime contributions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Infrared approximants and ultraviolet asymptotics test different parts of a candidate zeta spectrum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Low eigenvalues encode the finite-prime zero approximations, whereas high eigenvalues determine heat asymptotics; the divergent factorial heat expansion warns that ultraviolet agreement is asymptotic rather than a convergent reconstruction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A self-adjoint prolate extension matches the high-energy counting of zeta zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Restricting the prolate operator to the Sonin space yields discrete negative spectrum whose square-root Dirac family has the same ultraviolet behavior as zeta zeros, while the source carefully claims asymptotic matching rather than equality of spectra.
